bodega-catena-zapata.history: Nicola Catena, an Italian immigrant, planted his first Malbec vineyard in Mendoza in 1902. His grandson Nicolás Catena Zapata introduced European techniques and, from the early 1990s, championed high-altitude vineyards in the Uco Valley. Today the winery works with grapes from six estate vineyards, including Adrianna and La Pirámide.
highlights: Two wines from the Adrianna vineyard were the first South American wines to receive 100 points from The Wine Advocate.
Estate vineyards: Angélica, La Pirámide, Nicasia, Domingo, Adrianna and Angélica Sur.
Adrianna vineyard, planted in 1992 at 1,450 m a.s.l. in Gualtallary.
bodega-catena-zapata.flagship_grapes: Blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec and Cabernet Franc (Adrianna and Nicasia vineyards), 18 months in French oak; first vintage 1997

zuccardi-valle-de-uco.history: The Zuccardi family planted its first vineyard in 1963. In 2007 it planted its first own estates in Paraje Altamira (Uco Valley), and in 2016 it opened the Zuccardi Valle de Uco winery there.
highlights: World's Best Vineyards number one in 2019, 2020 and 2021; Hall of Fame in 2022.
Finca Piedra Infinita Gravascal 2022: 100 points from James Suckling (Argentina 2025 Tasting Report).
Alluvial soils with large stones and high calcium carbonate content, according to the winery.

casa-el-enemigo.history: El Enemigo is the project of winemaker Alejandro Vigil and historian Adrianna Catena, conceived in 2009. Its wines are made at Casa Vigil, in Chachingo (Maipú), where Bodega Aleanna produces the El Enemigo and Gran Enemigo ranges.
highlights: Gran Enemigo SV Gualtallary 2013: 100 points from The Wine Advocate, according to the winery
Gran Enemigo SV El Cepillo 2015: 98 points Descorchados and 97 Tim Atkin
In 2026 James Suckling awarded 100 points to two Gualtallary wines from the project
casa-el-enemigo.flagship_grapes: Cabernet Franc-based blends from Gualtallary, El Cepillo, Chacayes and Agrelo

durigutti-family-winemakers-finca-victor.history: Family winery founded in 2002 by winemaker brothers Héctor and Pablo Durigutti. From 2005 they assembled some 35 hectares in Las Compuertas (Luján de Cuyo), including century-old vineyards; this is home to Finca Victoria, open to visitors and with a guesthouse.
highlights: Century-old vineyards still in production in Las Compuertas, Luján de Cuyo
They grow varieties that are rare in Argentina, such as Cordisco and Nero d'Avola
High-density plantings of up to 9,200 vines per hectare

bodega-colome.history: Founded in 1831 by the governor of Salta, Nicolás Severo de Isasmendi; in 1854 his daughter Ascensión and José Benjamín Dávalos introduced pre-phylloxera Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon. Since 1998 it has belonged to Donald Hess, who steered it toward high-altitude wines. It describes itself as the oldest continuously producing winery in Argentina.
highlights: Vineyards on four estates: La Brava, Colomé, El Arenal and Altura Máxima (3,111 m a.s.l.)
The James Turrell Museum operates on the estate
Estancia Colomé, a nine-room boutique hotel among the vineyards
bodega-colome.flagship_grapes: Malbec from the Altura Máxima estate (3,111 m a.s.l.)

bodega-luigi-bosca.history: Founded in 1901 by Leoncio Arizu, of Basque descent, the winery remains in the hands of the Arizu family, now in its fourth generation. It has more than 700 hectares across seven estates, including Finca Los Nobles in Las Compuertas, whose vineyard dates from 1863.
highlights: New World Winery of the Year at Wine Enthusiast's 2025 Wine Star Awards.
Member of the DOC Luján de Cuyo.
Finca Los Nobles (Las Compuertas), its oldest vineyard, dates from 1863.

cheval-des-andes.history: Founded in 1999 as a project of Château Cheval Blanc, of Saint-Émilion, and Terrazas de los Andes, driven by Pierre Lurton and winemaker Roberto de la Mota. It makes a single blended wine from grapes grown in two vineyards: Las Compuertas, in Luján de Cuyo, and Altamira, in the Uco Valley.
highlights: Las Compuertas vineyard with ungrafted Malbec planted in 1929.
Alluvial soils: 48% limestone, 36% sand and 16% clay, according to Cheval Blanc.
It presents itself as the 'Grand Cru of the Andes'.
cheval-des-andes.flagship_grapes: Blend of Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon and Petit Verdot

vina-cobos.history: Founded in 1998 by American winemaker Paul Hobbs, it began almost as a project to study the potential of Malbec. The first Cobos Malbec was from the 1999 vintage. It works vineyards in Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley.
highlights: Cobos Malbec 2011: 100 points from James Suckling (2013), the first South American wine to receive that score.

bodega-kaiken.history: Founded in 2002 by Chilean winemaker Aurelio Montes, a founding partner of Viña Montes, who had visited Mendoza in 2000. The name refers to the caiquén, a goose that flies between Chile and Argentina. The winery is in Vistalba, surrounded by century-old vines.
highlights: Mai was its first icon wine; in the Pehuenche language it means 'first'.
Ramos Generales restaurant, with views of the Andes.
bodega-kaiken.flagship_grapes: Malbec from vines around 80 years old; aged in French oak

bodega-noemia-de-patagonia.history: It began as a joint project of Danish winemaker Hans Vinding-Diers and Countess Noemi Marone Cinzano, based in a 1952 winery in Mainqué. Today it is owned by Hans and his family and works a Malbec vineyard planted in 1932.
highlights: Pre-phylloxera Malbec vineyard planted in 1932, propagated by massal selection
Organic farming; sustainability certification in 2025, according to Diario Río Negro
Wine Advocate called Noemía 'the best wine in Río Negro'
bodega-noemia-de-patagonia.flagship_grapes: Malbec from a 1.5 ha ungrafted vineyard planted in 1932

bodega-lagarde.history: Founded in 1897 in Mayor Drummond by Captain José Ángel Pereira, it is one of Mendoza's century-old wineries. It has belonged to the Pescarmona family since 1969; today it is run by Sofía and Lucila Pescarmona, the third generation.
highlights: Zonda restaurant holds a MICHELIN star and a Green Star; Fogón is recognised by the MICHELIN Guide.
Certified B Corporation.
Member of the DOC Luján de Cuyo.
bodega-lagarde.flagship_grapes: Signature blend made in limited lots, only in exceptional vintages; first vintage (No. 1) 1990

bodega-el-porvenir-de-cafayate.history: The Romero family returned to winemaking after selling its Tolombón winery in the 1980s; Juan Carlos Romero bought an old winery in Cafayate and Finca El Retiro, with pergola-trained Torrontés vines over 80 years old. Lucía Romero Marcuzzi has run the company since 2013–2014.
highlights: Tim Atkin gave 98 points to Finca Alto Los Cuises Malbec 2024 (Argentina 2026 Special Report)
Paul Hobbs advises as consulting winemaker
It makes seven different styles of Torrontés
bodega-el-porvenir-de-cafayate.flagship_grapes: Top-of-the-range red blend (grapes not specified in the source)

achaval-ferrer.history: Founded in 1998 by Santiago Achával, Manuel Ferrer, Diego Rosso, Marcelo Victoria and Italian winemaker Roberto Cipresso. It became known for its single-vineyard Malbecs, such as Finca Altamira. It now belongs to a Russian holding company, and in 2019 it bought the Melipal winery in Agrelo.
highlights: Quimera Bistro restaurant, recommended by the Michelin Guide.
achaval-ferrer.flagship_grapes: Single-vineyard Malbec from Altamira (Uco Valley), old ungrafted vines

bodegas-caro.history: CARO is a partnership between Domaines Barons de Rothschild (Lafite) and the Catena family, bringing together Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon. The winery occupies a restored heritage cellar from 1884 in Godoy Cruz, with an art space called La NEF.
highlights: French-Argentine partnership between the Rothschilds of Lafite and the Catena family
Heritage cellar from 1884 in Godoy Cruz, 10 minutes from Mendoza
bodegas-caro.flagship_grapes: Blend of Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon

bodega-rutini.history: Felipe Rutini founded Bodega La Rural in Coquimbito, Maipú, in 1885. Around 1924–1925 he began planting in the Uco Valley, and in 2008 construction of the Rutini Wines winery in Tupungato began. The original Maipú building houses the Wine Museum.
highlights: Presents itself as a pioneering winery in the Uco Valley since 1925.
Wine Museum at the original site in Coquimbito, Maipú.
Winemaking led by Juan Pablo Murgia.

bodega-trivento.history: Trivento is the Argentine subsidiary of Concha y Toro and began in 1996. Its winery is in Maipú, with the Los Vientos restaurant, and its Casa Drummond hospitality centre is in Luján de Cuyo. It is among the country's leading exporters of bottled wine.
highlights: Eolo Malbec 2019: 95 points from Tim Atkin and from James Suckling
Casa Drummond won Best Of Wine Tourism Global Winner 2027, according to the winery
According to the winery, it is the best-selling Argentine wine brand in Europe
bodega-trivento.flagship_grapes: Malbec from a 1912 vineyard (4 ha, 983 m a.s.l.) on the Mendoza River; aged in French oak

bodega-el-esteco.history: Founded in 1892 in Cafayate by French brothers David and Salvador Michel. It preserves old vineyards of Criolla grapes and Torrontés more than 70 years old, and a winery in colonial architecture. The Patios de Cafayate hotel operates next to the winery.
highlights: Old vineyards of Criolla grapes and Torrontés more than 70 years old
Patios de Cafayate hotel, a 17th-century building with 32 rooms
Experiences: tour with tasting, horseback ride and Noches Mágicas
bodega-el-esteco.flagship_grapes: Blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec, Cabernet Franc and Merlot from Cafayate (2017 vintage: 55/30/10/5), 18 months in oak and 12 months in bottle

vina-dona-paula.history: Doña Paula began in 1997 with the purchase of its first vineyard in Ugarteche, Luján de Cuyo, and later added estates in Gualtallary, Altamira and Los Cerezos. It uses only estate-grown grapes, and its Terroir in Focus programme studies soils and climates.
highlights: Selección de Bodega has been made since 2015 solely from Finca Alluvia grapes, Gualtallary.
More than 160 wines rated 90 points or higher, according to its tourism listing.
vina-dona-paula.flagship_grapes: Malbec from Finca Alluvia, Gualtallary (1,350 m a.s.l.); 24 months in French oak

bodega-alta-vista.history: It operates in an 1899 building in Chacras de Coria, restored with respect for its architecture, with an original cellar from 1900. It is one of the oldest wineries still producing in Mendoza. It is run by Patrick d'Aulan, heir to a French winemaking tradition, and makes wines from Mendoza and Salta.
highlights: Building regarded as part of Mendoza's historical heritage, according to the winery.
Assemblage restaurant, with a seven-course menu.
bodega-alta-vista.flagship_grapes: Blend of Malbec (80%) and Cabernet Sauvignon (20%), 18 months in new French oak (1999 vintage)

casa-vigil.history: The Vigil family opened Casa Vigil in 2015 in Chachingo (Maipú). It combines a restaurant, art and a tour inspired by Dante's Divine Comedy. On the same property, Bodega Aleanna makes the El Enemigo and Gran Enemigo wines.
highlights: Themed tour through hell, purgatory and paradise, inspired by the Divine Comedy
Three-course lunches and seven- and fourteen-course dinners with wine pairing
casa-vigil.flagship_grapes: Cabernet Franc-based blends from different parajes of Mendoza

bodega-chacra.history: Founded in 2004 by Piero Incisa della Rocchetta, grandson of the creator of Sassicaia, who bought an abandoned winery in Mainqué with vineyards planted from 1932 onward. Burgundian Jean-Marc Roulot collaborated on the planting and the first Chardonnay harvest.
highlights: Ungrafted vineyards planted in 1932 and 1955
Low-intervention winemaking in the Alto Valle del Río Negro

bodega-otronia.history: A project of Alejandro Bulgheroni in Sarmiento, Chubut, on the shores of Lake Musters, presented as the southernmost vineyard in the country. The first vines were planted in 2010, the first harvest was in 2017, and today it farms 52 organic hectares.
highlights: Otronia Chardonnay, Best White Wine of Argentina in Descorchados 2024
Otronia Malbec 2021: 98 points in Descorchados
It lies within the Sarmiento GI, recognised by the INV in 2023
bodega-otronia.flagship_grapes: Chardonnay; named Best White Wine of Argentina in Descorchados 2024

bodega-antigal.history: A winery in Russell (Maipú) whose main building dates from 1897. It was bought in 1999 and remodelled by the Bormida & Yanzon studio, moving it from bulk wine to the premium segment under the Antigal brand. The first vintage of One was 2005.
highlights: Wine Enthusiast named it New World Winery of the Year (2023)
One of the oldest wineries in Mendoza still in production
Has exported to the United States since 2007

pulenta-estate.history: Brothers Eduardo and Hugo Pulenta, third generation of a winemaking family of Italian origin, founded the winery in 2002 in Alto Agrelo. The building, by the Bórmida & Yanzón studio, keeps the wines in an underground cellar with a natural temperature of 14 to 17 °C.
highlights: According to the winery, it pioneered Cabernet Franc in Argentina (Forbes Argentina).

pyros-wines.history: A Grupo Salentein project in the Pedernal Valley, driven by its founder Mijndert Pon, who arrived in the valley in 2008. Before planting, he studied the land with more than 200 soil pits and identified seven soil profiles, mostly calcareous. The name comes from the Greek for 'fire', alluding to flint (pedernal).
highlights: Block 4 Malbec 2015: Red Wine Trophy at the 16th Korea Wine Challenge
Certified organic vineyard (iProfesional, 2024)
Calcareous soils; Limestone Hill comes from prehistoric limestone rock
pyros-wines.flagship_grapes: Malbec from a calcareous plot in the Pedernal Valley (San Juan), ~1,400 m

finca-las-moras.history: A San Juan winery of Grupo Peñaflor created in 2001 as an export project: its first sale was to Belgium and it reached the Argentine market around 2002. In 2007 it launched Alma Mora, which the press presents as the best-selling Malbec in Argentina.
highlights: Exports to more than 50 countries (MDZ, 2025)
Has its own vineyard in the Pedernal Valley, San Juan
Director of Viticulture and Oenology: Marcelo Belmonte (Tiempo de San Juan, 2021)
finca-las-moras.flagship_grapes: Syrah from several San Juan valleys, expressing Pedernal

bodega-corazon-del-sol.history: Dr. Revana, owner of wineries in Napa and Oregon, arrived in Mendoza in 2008 and that year planted the first vines of Rhône varieties in western Tunuyán. In 2023 it obtained organic certification, and in 2024 it opened a tasting room in the city of Mendoza.
highlights: A pioneer of Rhône varieties (Grenache, Mourvèdre, Syrah) at altitude.
Gran Reserva Malbec 2016: number 74 in the Wine Spectator Top 100 2019.
Certified organic since 2023.

finca-sophenia.history: Founded in 1998 by Roberto Luka, former president of Wines of Argentina, it was among the first to plant in Gualtallary. The name combines Sophia and Eugenia, the founders' daughter. It makes estate wines with sustainable and organic viticulture.
highlights: One of the first estates planted in Gualtallary (1998).
130 ha at 1,200 m on stony, calcareous soils.
Roberto Luka was named Agribusiness Entrepreneur of the Year in 2016.
finca-sophenia.flagship_grapes: Plot selection from Gualtallary; grapes not specified on the page consulted

the-vines-of-mendoza.history: Michael Evans and Pablo Giménez Riili founded the project in 2004 and bought land in Los Chacayes. It is a private-vineyard venture: by 2008 it had more than 230 owners. In 2011 it opened tasting rooms, and in 2014 the hotel The Vines Resort & Spa.
highlights: More than 230 private vineyard owners who make their own wine.
The Vines Resort & Spa: 33 private villas, opened in 2014.
An estate of about 1,500 acres (around 600 ha) in Los Chacayes.

bodega-cuvelier-los-andes.history: The Cuvelier family, with a wine house in France since 1804 and owner of Château Léoville-Poyferré, came to the Uco Valley in 1998 with Baptiste Cuvelier and the advice of Michel Rolland. It is part of the Clos de los Siete project in Vista Flores.
highlights: Organic and biodynamic viticulture, according to the winery.
Sandy soils with alluvial stones; 20 °C diurnal temperature range.
Member of Clos de los Siete alongside Monteviejo, Rolland and DiamAndes.
bodega-cuvelier-los-andes.flagship_grapes: Barrel-selection blend, aged in French oak

clos-de-los-siete.history: A project created by Michel Rolland and Jean-Michel Arcaute, who bought more than 800 ha in Vista Flores and divided them among partner wineries. Today its members are Monteviejo, Rolland, Cuvelier Los Andes and DiamAndes. The Clos de los Siete wine has been made since 2003 from estate grapes.
highlights: Blend made by Michel Rolland solely from estate grapes.
About 10 km of flood defences in Vista Flores.
Soils of rounded stones, clay and sand.
clos-de-los-siete.flagship_grapes: Majority-Malbec blend with Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Petit Verdot and Cabernet Franc; French oak

domaine-nico.history: Laura Catena's project devoted solely to single-plot Pinot Noir in the Uco Valley. It is named after her daughter Nicola, which in turn recalls Nicola Catena, who founded Catena Zapata in 1902. Since 2016 it has bottled five plots separately, in Villa Bastías and Gualtallary.
highlights: Five single-plot Pinot Noirs: Grand Mère, Grand Père, Histoire d'A, La Savante and Le Paradis.
Plots in Villa Bastías (1,120 m) and Gualtallary (1,350–1,500 m), Tupungato.
First Pinot Noir planting in Villa Bastías in 1993, according to the winery.

bodega-sottano.history: The Sottano family has made wine since 1890, when Fioravante Sottano, one of the pioneers of Mendoza winemaking, settled there. Today it produces premium wines from vineyards located mainly in Perdriel.
bodega-sottano.flagship_grapes: Malbec and Blend; fermented in closed French oak barrels

bodega-pascual-toso.history: Piedmontese Pascual Toso founded his first winery in 1890 in San José, Guaymallén. In the early 20th century he bought vineyards in Maipú and built the Las Barrancas winery, where it now makes sparkling, white and red wines.
highlights: Best Argentine Producer Trophy at the IWSC in London (2007)
More than 220 ha of its own in Barrancas, Maipú, at about 750 m a.s.l.
Exports to almost 30 markets, according to the winery
bodega-pascual-toso.flagship_grapes: Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon blend from Barrancas, barrel selection

finca-flichman.history: Founded in 1910 by Sami Flichman, an immigrant from Łódź (Poland), on the stony soils of Barrancas (Maipú). In 1947 his son Isaac and winemaker Raúl de la Mota created Caballero de la Cepa. Since the late 1990s it has belonged to the Portuguese company Sogrape.
highlights: Caballero de la Cepa (1947), one of the first Argentine premium wines to achieve international success
Isaac Flichman introduced Syrah from France, according to iProfesional
finca-flichman.flagship_grapes: Top range: Malbec and Gran Corte (blend with Cabernet Sauvignon) from Uco Valley vineyards

bodega-rolland.history: The winery of French oenologist Michel Rolland and his wife Dany in Vista Flores, within Clos de los Siete, a project created in 1999. It makes the Mariflor range, from the highest plot on the property, and Val de Flores, from a Malbec vineyard more than 80 years old.
highlights: Val de Flores: 10 ha of old Malbec, first vintage at its own winery in 2010.
Member of the Clos de los Siete project in Vista Flores.
Visits by reservation only.
bodega-rolland.flagship_grapes: Selection of grapes from the Mariflor estate

bodegas-lopez.history: José Gregorio López Rivas arrived from Málaga in 1886 and in 1898 began making wine with his brothers in General Gutiérrez (Maipú). The winery remains in the hands of the founding family, now in its fourth generation, with a style of long-aged wines.
highlights: Montchenot 20 años 2002: 95 points Tim Atkin and 95 Descorchados
Capacity of 40 million litres; 5.7 million in French oak casks
Keeps bottles from vintages dating back to 1938
bodegas-lopez.flagship_grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot (Cabernet-dominant) from the La Marthita estate, vines planted in 1940

bodega-cruzat.history: Founded in 2004 by a group of Chilean businessmen and Argentine agronomist and winemaker Pedro Federico Rosell, it specialises in premium sparkling wines. They are made by the traditional method, with second fermentation in bottle.
highlights: Winery devoted exclusively to traditional-method sparkling wines.
bodega-cruzat.flagship_grapes: 80% Pinot Noir, 20% Chardonnay; traditional-method sparkling wine with extended lees ageing

huarpe-riglos-family-wines.history: It brings together two wineries: Huarpe, created in 2003 by the Hernández Toso brothers with an estate in Agrelo, and Riglos, owned by the Werthein group, with a vineyard in Gualtallary. Winemaker José Hernández Toso is the great-grandson of Pascual Toso, a pioneer of Argentine winemaking.
highlights: Gran Corte Riglos 2009, named wine of the year by Wine Enthusiast in 2012.
Holds the only original fragment of the Berlin Wall in Mendoza.
huarpe-riglos-family-wines.flagship_grapes: 34% Malbec, 33% Cabernet Sauvignon, 33% Cabernet Franc; 18 months in French oak barrels and foudres (Finca Las Divas, Gualtallary)

fabre-montmayou.history: Winery of Frenchman Hervé Joyaux Fabre, who settled in Vistalba and built the winery with his wife, Diane. It makes French-style reds and, according to Revista Mercado, produces about 50,000 cases a year.
highlights: Its Grand Vin won an award at the Bourg-Blaye competition, Bordeaux (Revista Mercado).
fabre-montmayou.flagship_grapes: Blend of 85% Malbec, 10% Cabernet Sauvignon and 5% Merlot (2006 vintage)

bodega-teho.history: Teho is the founding brand of Mil Suelos, the group of Alejandro Sejanovich, Jeff Mausbach and Jorge Crotta. Its first vintage was 2010, and its flagship vineyard is Tomal, in La Consulta, planted in 1940. The name means 'blood' in the Huarpe language.
highlights: Tomal vineyard: four hectares in La Consulta, planted in 1940.
Top range Teho Grand Cru, with three selection wines from the Tomal vineyard.
It also makes the Zaha range (Malbec, Cabernet Franc, Marsanne, Sémillon, among others).
bodega-teho.flagship_grapes: Selections from the Tomal vineyard, La Consulta (planted in 1940); grapes and ageing not specified

bodegas-bianchi.history: Founded in 1928 by Italian immigrant Valentín Bianchi in San Rafael; his son Enzo consolidated it as Bodegas Bianchi. In 1995 it opened the Champañera Bianchi, and in 2018 it added a winery in the Uco Valley. Today it is run by the family, with the fourth generation joining.
highlights: Famiglia Bianchi Reserva Malbec 2012 won the Trophée at Vinalies Internationales Paris 2014.
The Champañera Bianchi, opened in 1995, receives more than 55,000 visitors a year.
Present in more than 40 countries, according to Mendoza Turismo.
bodegas-bianchi.flagship_grapes: Top-of-the-range line: red blend (Grand Cru) and Chardonnay

zorzal-wines.history: Uco Valley winery with a vineyard in Gualtallary (Tupungato), at 1,350 m altitude. It makes the Terroir Único, Gran Terroir, Eggo, Parcelario and Conceptuales ranges, with labels such as El Barba, Piantao, Porfiado and Filoso Pinot Noir.
highlights: Has fermented and aged the Eggo range in concrete eggs since 2011.
Organic farming and native yeasts; vineyard in Gualtallary at about 1,350 m.

penedo-borges.history: A boutique winery founded by Brazilian and Argentine friends in Alto Agrelo, focused on premium wines in small quantities. It farms a single 48-hectare vineyard at 1,050 m a.s.l. under sustainable management.
highlights: Gold at Best Of Mendoza's Wine Tourism 2024, Small Wineries category.
penedo-borges.flagship_grapes: Malbec (85%) with Cabernet Sauvignon and Petit Verdot; selection of the best barrels

finca-aniello.history: Winery founded in 2012 in Mainqué on a historic farm with a 1927 building, the former Podlesch winery. It works vineyards from 1932 and 1947, with Malbec, ungrafted Trousseau and Pinot Noir; its 006 range takes its name from the founding estate.
highlights: Vineyards planted in 1932 and 1947; pre-phylloxera Malbec from massal selection
006 Riverside Estate range, named after the founding estate

huichaira-vineyards.history: A high-altitude vineyard in Huichaira, Quebrada de Humahuaca, with 4 ha at 2,710 m a.s.l. Its first vintages, including a co-fermented blend, were made in 2018 at Amanecer Andino with winemaker Alejandro Sejanovich.
highlights: Winemaker: Alejandro Sejanovich
First co-fermented blend of Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah (2018)
Quebrada de Humahuaca GI (recognised in 2015)
huichaira-vineyards.flagship_grapes: Red (blend); grapes not specified in the source

bodega-san-pedro-de-yacochuya.history: A project Arnaldo Etchart launched in 1995, after selling Bodegas Etchart, in partnership with French oenologist Michel Rolland. The estate is at 2,035 m a.s.l. in Yacochuya, above Cafayate. Today it is run by the Etchart siblings.
highlights: 16 ha: 9 of Malbec, 4 of Cabernet Sauvignon, 2 of Torrontés and 1 of Tannat
San Pedro de Yacochuya: 85% Malbec and 15% Cabernet Sauvignon
The label bears a cardón cactus and Michel Rolland's signature
bodega-san-pedro-de-yacochuya.flagship_grapes: Premium red; about 15 months in new French oak barrels

bodega-domingo-molina.history: A winery founded by the three sons of Osvaldo 'Palo' Domingo, creator of Domingo Hermanos, who added their mother's surname, Molina. It focuses on premium wines from its own estates in Yacochuya, Cafayate and Animaná, between 1,500 and 2,200 m a.s.l.
highlights: Finca El Rupestre at 2,200 m a.s.l.
Mortero white and red blends, and the sweet wine Martes 13
Guided tours and tastings every day from 10 am to 5 pm
bodega-domingo-molina.flagship_grapes: Malbec 80%, Merlot 10%, Tannat 10%; 12 months in oak (2011 vintage)

bodega-santiago-graffigna.history: Founded in 1870 by Genoese immigrants, it is the oldest winery in San Juan and the third oldest in Argentina. It passed through Pernod Ricard and in 2019 was bought by the Chilean group VSPT (CCU), with vineyards in Pocito, Cañada Honda and La Consulta. The Santiago Graffigna Museum has operated there since 2003.
highlights: Wine museum opened in November 2003
200,000-litre French oak vat, dating from around 1900
Top range Glorious Selection (Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon)
bodega-santiago-graffigna.flagship_grapes: Premium range with Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon (grapes from the Uco Valley and Cañada Honda, San Juan)

cara-sur.history: A project born in 2011 in the Calingasta valley to rescue old pergola-trained vineyards and traditional techniques in the paraje of Hilario. It was founded by mountaineer Francisco Bugallo and Sebastián Zuccardi together with their wives. It farms about 10 ha on four estates, between 1,550 and 1,700 m.
highlights: Works old pergola-trained vineyards of Criolla Chica, Bonarda and Barbera in the paraje of Hilario
Part of the official San Juan Wine Route (Calingasta)
cara-sur.flagship_grapes: Red blend of Italian varieties from old vines in Hilario

trapiche-costa-y-pampa.history: In 2009 Trapiche bought land on the Santa Isabel estancia in Chapadmalal, about 6 km from the sea and 30 km from Mar del Plata, and developed a maritime-climate vineyard there. It has 26 hectares with varieties such as Albariño, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir and Riesling.
highlights: Albariño 2022: 95 points from Tim Atkin, Best Albariño of Argentina (2023)
Vineyard about 6 km from the Atlantic Ocean, in Chapadmalal
trapiche-costa-y-pampa.flagship_grapes: Albariño from a coastal vineyard in Chapadmalal

sineres-champanera.history: A project of Agustín Sommavilla and Andrea Fissore in Villa General Belgrano, with vineyards in Costa Verde, the Sommavilla family estate. Since 2017 it has focused on white wines and traditional-method sparkling wines, which went on sale in 2021.
highlights: Traditional-method sparkling wines, about 10,000 bottles a year
Chardonnay Brut Nature 2018 awarded by Tim Atkin
sineres-champanera.flagship_grapes: Chardonnay, traditional method; 2018 vintage awarded by Tim Atkin

highlights: Registered with the INV as '35.cinco Vinos de Montaña', in Calingasta
Offers vineyard visits and tastings of high-altitude wines by reservation

adamow.history: Pedro Adamow, from Mar del Plata, bought the smallholding in Lago Puelo in late 2007, and in 2009 the first vines arrived from Mendoza. After about 13 years he produced his first bottle; he makes Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc on about 2 hectares.
highlights: About 5,500 to 6,000 bottles a year of Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc
Vineyard visits and tastings year-round

aguma-casa-vinicola.history: A family venture of winemaker Óscar Biondolillo, formerly of Graffigna and technical director of Callia, and chemical engineer Marisol Salvador. It started in a shed in Pocito, moved through rented wineries, and for about 15 years has had its own premises in Marquesado. The name combines those of their children, Agustina and Matías.
highlights: Portfolio of 16 wines in four ranges, including a sparkling wine
Plans a top-of-the-range wine: La Ciénaga Syrah 2025, in barrel and concrete egg

aleste-bodega-vinedos.history: A project begun in 1999 in Médanos, in the south of Buenos Aires province, about 40 km from the Atlantic; in 2000 an experimental plot with nine varieties was planted, and the first vintage was 2006. Italian oenologist Alberto Antonini led the project.
highlights: Sandy soils over limestone, about 40 km from the sea
Chardonnay awarded a silver medal at the Decanter World Wine Awards 2009

alfa-crux.history: A winery of modern architecture in La Consulta, with several interconnected buildings, now owned by Agostino Wine Group. Its vineyards are in El Cepillo, at almost 1,200 m, and it has the Crux Cocina restaurant.
highlights: Alfa Crux Malbec: limited edition with 18 months in French oak.
Crux Cocina restaurant, a mountain bistro with views of the Andes.
Vineyards in El Cepillo, San Carlos, at almost 1,200 m.
alfa-crux.flagship_grapes: Malbec; 18 months in French oak and 12 in bottle

algodon-wine-estates.history: An estate in Cuadro Benegas with vineyards planted from the 1940s, turned into a complex comprising a boutique winery, hotel, golf course and real estate development. It was assembled by Scott Mathis and partners; the winemaker is Mauro Nosenzo, advised by Master of Wine Anthony Foster.
highlights: Vineyards dating back to 1946, irrigated with snowmelt, on sandy loam and clay soils.
Chez Gastón restaurant, 8-room hotel, golf and tennis on the estate.
Estate of 830 hectares, according to Bonvivir.

alpasion.history: The project began with a visit to the Uco Valley in 2009 and was formally established in March 2010 in Los Chacayes. Its first wine was the 2011 Malbec, and the lodge welcomed its first guests in 2012. It practises certified organic farming.
highlights: Organic certification, according to the winery.
Alpasión Lodge with rooms, glamping and agritourism; Iris restaurant.
Winemaker: Ezequiel Manoni.

altocedro.history: A La Consulta winery founded in 1998, housed in a 19th-century building. Its winemaker is Karim Mussi Saffie, and it makes limited-production wines from old vines.
highlights: Winery in a 19th-century building in La Consulta.

altos-del-gualeguaychu-bodega-ianni.history: Vilma and Néstor Ianni left Chovet, Santa Fe, and in 2001 settled on a smallholding in Colonia El Potrero, Gualeguaychú. In 2012 they planted 1.5 hectares of Viognier, Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Franc, later added Tannat and opened an INV-licensed winery.
highlights: Restaurant-bar opened in 2019 with tastings and farm produce
INV-licensed winery in Colonia El Potrero, Gualeguaychú

altura-de-los-vinedos.history: A project of Diego Espinoza in Fiambalá, who began making his own wines in 2010 after working at another winery in the area. It has no vineyards: it buys grapes from growers in Fiambalá and Medanitos. He is building his winery in adobe, with a capacity of 45,000 litres.
highlights: Makes wine from purchased grapes from Fiambalá (1,505 m) and Medanitos (1,900 m)
Adobe winery with a capacity of 45,000 litres
Works with Bonarda, Malbec, Syrah, Cabernet and uva chinche

amanecer-andino.history: A family winery near Purmamarca, in the Quebrada de Humahuaca, which Alfredo González and his son started as a hobby around 2009. It is reached by a footbridge over the Río Grande. Its wines are made by winemaker Lucas Niven.
highlights: Winemaker: Lucas Niven
Makes a Bonarda and Cabernet Sauvignon blend and a Sauvignon Blanc from Tumbaya
Quebrada de Humahuaca GI (recognised in 2015)

anaia-wines.history: Anaia was born in 2016, when its partners bought a 72-hectare estate in Agrelo with the idea of a domaine: making wine only from its own grapes. The estate is at 960 m a.s.l., in one of the coolest parts of Agrelo.
highlights: International Gold in the Great Wine Capitals Best Of awards, Architecture and Landscapes.

antigua-bodega.history: An urban winery in the city of San Juan, housed in a historic building that sheltered local residents after the 1944 earthquake. Luis Víctor Chirino invested in the property in 1990, and the winery opened in 1994, with its own museum and an art gallery of the family collection.
highlights: Own museum and art gallery with the Chirino family collection
Building considered a city monument for its role in the 1944 earthquake

antiguo-legado.history: A vineyard and winery in Paraje Macedo, about 30 km from General Madariaga, where cultivation began in 2020. It works four red varieties: Pinot Noir, Marselan, Tannat and Petit Verdot.
highlights: Visits by reservation: technical tour of the vineyard and winery with tasting

antucura.history: French publisher Anne-Caroline Biancheri bought the Vista Flores estate in 1998 and between 2000 and 2005 planted 100 ha of red varieties, advised by Michel Rolland. In 2005 she opened an inn on the estate.
highlights: 100 ha of Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Petit Verdot, Cabernet Franc, Syrah and Pinot Noir.
Oenological consulting by Michel Rolland.
Small inn opened in 2005.

ayestaran-allard.history: A winery in the Comarca Andina, in El Hoyo, Chubut, with 4 hectares planted on plots bought from Patagonian Wines. It makes its own wines and those of small neighbouring growers, as well as a sparkling wine.
highlights: Makes and bottles wines for small growers in the Comarca Andina
Donated Gewürztraminer cuttings to neighbouring growers

bardas-al-sur.history: A project of Roberto Barragán on a family smallholding in Gaiman, in the lower valley of the Chubut River. After trials begun in 2010, he ordered the vines in 2012 and started producing in 2020; Pinot Noir and Malbec were the varieties that performed best.
highlights: Vineyard in the lower valley of the Chubut River, in Gaiman
bardas-al-sur.flagship_grapes: Malbec with six months in French oak and three in American oak

highlights: Part of the Camino del Vino of Río Negro, in Cipolletti
Organises an annual music series together with Humberto Canale and Agrestis

bodega-a16.history: Bodega A16 was born in 2007 as the 16th venture of businessman Gerardo Cartellone, whose family's winemaking tradition goes back to his Sicilian great-grandfather. Its Papa Francisco vineyard is in Perdriel, at 950 m a.s.l., on alluvial soils with rounded river stones.
highlights: Alluvial sandy-loam soils with rounded river stones, according to the winery.
bodega-a16.flagship_grapes: Malbec, 24 months in French oak barrels

bodega-agrestis.history: A General Roca winery owned by a long-established Alto Valle family, with vines brought from France. It makes traditional-method sparkling wines and still wines from Pinot Noir, Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec and Chardonnay.
highlights: Organises an annual music series together with Humberto Canale and La Falda

bodega-aicardi.history: A winery owned by the Aicardi family in San Patricio del Chañar, Neuquén, focused on high-quality wines made in small quantities.

bodega-alfredo-roca.history: The Roca family has grown vines in San Rafael since 1912. In 1976 winemaker Alfredo Roca bought a winery built in 1905 in Cañada Seca and launched the family project bearing his name. Today it is run by his children Alejandro, Graciela and Carolina.
highlights: Original 1905 winery with two preserved halls and a third added in the same style.
The Roca family has been settled in San Rafael since 1912.

bodega-alpamanta.history: Founded in 2005 by European partners in Ugarteche, it has practised biodynamic agriculture from the outset. Its name means 'love for the land' in a local native language. Its vineyards and wines are certified organic and biodynamic.
highlights: Organic (Ecocert), biodynamic (Demeter) and vegan certifications.
Global Gold in the 2024 Great Wine Capitals Best Of awards.

bodega-alto-limay.history: A boutique winery in Cuadro Benegas, San Rafael, with its own vineyards irrigated by the Atuel and Diamante rivers. It states that it farms organically with biodynamic tools; the winemaker is Oscar Zalazar.
highlights: Offers paired tastings and a 'winemaker for a day' experience.

bodega-altos-la-cienaga.history: A family winery in Colalao del Valle founded in 1940 by Javier Julián Díaz. It began with traditional vino patero and today also makes a range of young wines, Don Javier, and age-worthy wines, La Ciénaga Altos.
highlights: Part of the Ruta del Vino de Altura of Tucumán
Makes vino patero, trodden by foot

bodega-amalaya.history: Founded in 2010 in Cafayate by Larissa and Christoph Ehrbar, children of Donald and Ursula Hess, owners of Colomé, to make fresher, lighter wines. It has 25 ha planted on Finca San Isidro and vineyards in Las Mercedes.
highlights: Sustainably farmed vineyards from the outset, according to the winery
Wine bar and restaurant with views of the hills
25 ha planted on Finca San Isidro
bodega-amalaya.flagship_grapes: Malbec 85%, Cabernet Sauvignon 10%, Tannat 5%; 12 months in French oak

bodega-argana.history: A boutique winery in San Rafael focused on reds, varietals and blends, with vineyards irrigated by snowmelt from the Atuel River. It grows Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
highlights: Capacity of 255,000 litres in stainless steel tanks.
Sells mainly on the domestic market, with limited editions in Europe, the US and Brazil.

bodega-argentia.history: A family winery in Gutiérrez (Maipú), founded in 1880 according to Turismo de Mendoza, one of the oldest in the department. It is run by its owners and offers tours, tastings and a restaurant.

bodega-artesanal-de-la-tierrita.history: An artisanal family winery in El Maitén, Eugenio Bustos, with an agroecological vineyard. It makes small-scale wines as naturally as possible.
highlights: Agroecological vineyard and small-scale wines.
Visits with a vineyard tour, tasting and optional asado.

bodega-artesanal-el-milagro.history: An artisanal winery in Albardón that is part of the San Juan Wine Route. It offers a tour of the whole process, from the organic vineyard to winemaking, with a tasting in the Don Juan cellar, and also has a cured-meats factory.
highlights: Guided tour with tasting in the Don Juan cellar
Organically managed vineyard, according to the official tourism portal

bodega-araoz-de-lamadrid.history: A project of Goyo and Ana Aráoz de Lamadrid in San Javier, Traslasierra, with about 10 hectares of Malbec and Syrah. It combines a winery, lodging and a cactus garden with some 450 species.
highlights: Cactus garden with some 450 species on the property
Weekend guided tours with a tasting of three wines

bodega-atamisque.history: Winery founded in 2007 by John du Monceau and his wife Chantal in San José, Tupungato, at 1,300 m. Under a stone roof, it makes wine by gravity flow, producing about 500,000 bottles a year of the Serbal, Catalpa and Atamisque ranges.
highlights: Known as 'the winery with the stone roof'; gravity-flow winemaking.
Exports 40% to more than 30 countries.
Part of Tierras de Atamisque, with a lodge, villas, golf and dining.
bodega-atamisque.flagship_grapes: Blend of Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Petit Verdot from Tupungato (Uco Valley); 14 months in new French oak

bodega-atilio-avena.history: A family winery in Russell (Maipú) founded by Don Atilio Avena, son of Piedmontese immigrants. For three generations it has made barrel-aged wines, and it also produces olive oil.
highlights: Three family generations; tour of olive groves and vineyards with tasting

bodega-augusto-pulenta.history: It emerged after the Pulenta family sold its stake in Peñaflor in 1997: Mario Pulenta kept vineyards and an old property in San Martín and created the winery there. The main building dates from 1901, with adobe walls and French pitch-pine structures.
highlights: 1901 main building with one of the oldest water mills in the area
Production capacity of close to 1.5 million litres
Valbona Varietales and Valbona Tradición brands

bodega-aureum-terra.history: A winery in Animaná, about 10 km from Cafayate, whose vineyards can be seen from Ruta 40. It makes wine from vines more than 50 years old.
highlights: Vineyards more than 50 years old

bodega-belasco-de-baquedano.history: The Belasco family, of Navarrese origin and owner of the La Navarra group, looked for vineyards in Chile and Argentina from 1999. In 2003 it bought a 65-hectare estate in Agrelo with vines planted in 1910 and began building the winery.
highlights: Vineyard with vines planted in 1910 in Agrelo.
Exports about 95% of its production.

bodega-benegas.history: Federico Benegas Lynch founded the winery in 1999 by buying back Finca Libertad, a vineyard planted by his great-grandfather Tiburcio Benegas, with vines 60 to 120 years old. He restored a 1900 building in Luján de Cuyo and added Finca La Encerrada, in Gualtallary.
highlights: Underground cellar 8 metres deep with stone walls.
Finca Libertad, with vines 60 to 120 years old.
bodega-benegas.flagship_grapes: Malbec, Cabernet Franc and an old-vine blend; lot selection, 18 months in new barrels

bodega-bombal.history: The family's winemaking history begins in 1892, when it planted Malbec in Lunlunta (Maipú) and built an adobe winery that still stands. Today, after five generations, it welcomes visitors on tours that begin in its historic vineyards.
highlights: Winery built entirely of adobe in 1892
Five generations and more than 130 harvests in Lunlunta, Maipú

bodega-bombal-y-aldao.history: It operates at Finca Los Álamos, an estancia built in 1830 by the Bombal family and restored in the 1930s by writer Susana Bombal, who hosted Borges there. The winery was renovated in 2006 and specialises in barrel ageing and custom wines.
highlights: Personalised barrel programme: the client chooses varietals and ageing times.
The estate includes a maze planted in 2003 in homage to Borges.

bodega-bonfanti.history: A family winery built in 2004 by Roberto Bonfanti, a descendant of Italian grape growers who arrived in 1915. Its vineyards are in Perdriel, one kilometre south of the Mendoza River, on old riverbeds with shallow soils.
highlights: Four generations of vine-growing tradition, according to the winery.

bodega-bournett.history: A family project born in 1997 with the 'Dijon' estate in San Rafael, later joined by the 'Fundadora' estate. The name pays tribute to ancestors who made wine in France. It works with small production volumes.
highlights: It has an Aroma Room for visitors, which it presents as unique in southern Mendoza.

bodega-boutique-las-carolinas.history: A boutique winery in Anillaco, Castro Barros department, included in the 2024 official list of tourist wineries of La Rioja. It is open every day for wine sales.

bodega-boutique-vinas-de-segisa.history: A winery in La Rinconada, Pocito, founded in 1906 and restored by its current owners, who preserved the adobe walls and cane-and-mud roofs. It retains lagares for vino patero, underground cellars with a spiral staircase and two French oak casks from 1860.
highlights: Two French oak casks 4 m in diameter made in 1860
Underground cellars and old lagares for vino patero

bodega-budeguer.history: The Budeguer family, from Tucumán, began in 2005 by buying land and planting vineyards in Maipú, and brought in its first harvest in 2008. Its 4000 range bears Tucumán's postcode. The Agrelo winery has an underground barrel room and an art gallery.

bodega-buonob.history: A family company in San Martín that makes organic wines. It claims a winemaking tradition of eight generations, first in Italy and then in Argentina.

bodega-cabrini.history: Don Leandro Cabrini, an Italian immigrant, planted his first 6 hectares of Malbec in Perdriel in 1918 and built the winery in 1920. Today it is run by the fifth family generation, and the founder's original house is preserved.
highlights: Fifth family generation; Victoria Cabrini is the winery's oenologist.

bodega-caelum.history: Caelum is a family project that began making wine in 2009, after more than ten years devoted to growing grapes on its Agrelo estate. It has also produced pistachios since 1994 and makes about 70,000 bottles a year, all from its own grapes.

bodega-carinae.history: Carinae was created by French couple Brigitte and Philippe Subra, who arrived in Mendoza in 1998 and restored an abandoned winery in Cruz de Piedra (Maipú). Today it is run by a young family and preserves an original vineyard from 1900.
highlights: Original 1900 vineyard and 90-year-old Arauco olive trees on the estate
Alluvial and clay loam soils, at about 850 m a.s.l.

bodega-carmelo-patti.history: A boutique family company devoted to age-worthy wines, which spend two to five years in bottle at the winery before release.

bodega-carmine-granata.history: Carmine Granata, an Italian immigrant, started the winery in 1930 in Mayor Drummond and came to produce 10 million litres from his own grapes in Luján de Cuyo and Maipú. Today it is run by his descendants.
highlights: Small museum with old winery and farm machinery.

bodega-cerro-el-pelao.history: A winery in Tafí del Valle included in the Ruta del Vino de Altura of Tucumán. According to the official tourism guide, it does not receive tourist visits.

bodega-chanarmuyo.history: Winery in the Chañarmuyo valley, in Famatina, at 1,720 m a.s.l. It welcomes visitors for tastings Monday to Saturday and has a guesthouse and a restaurant serving regional cuisine. Its brands are Chañarmuyo and Chamas Honnorat.
highlights: Vineyards at 1,720 m a.s.l. in the Chañarmuyo valley
Guesthouse on the estate
bodega-chanarmuyo.flagship_grapes: Tannat from the Famatina Valley, at more than 1,700 m a.s.l. (ageing not published)

bodega-chico-zossi.history: A winery with a family tradition in Colalao del Valle, presented by Tucumán's official tourism board as a pioneer in the province. It sells on the domestic market and in neighbouring countries.
highlights: Considered a pioneering winery of Tucumán by the provincial tourism board

bodega-claroscuro.history: Founded in 2011 by Paula and Gustavo Cucchiara in Vista Flores, it presents itself as a winery-gallery that combines art and wine. It has 46 ha on several estates in Gualtallary, Vista Flores, Agua Amarga, Paraje Altamira and El Cepillo.
highlights: It presents itself as the only winery-art gallery in Argentina.
46 ha on five Uco Valley estates, between 1,050 and 1,400 m.
Uncommon varieties such as Nero d'Avola and Pinot Grigio in Vista Flores.

bodega-clos-de-chacras.history: Founded in 1921 by the Gargantini family in Chacras de Coria, it is now carried on by Silvia Gargantini, the founder's granddaughter, and her husband Alejandro Genoud. It makes wine in traditional concrete vats with modern equipment and also has vineyards in Gualtallary.
bodega-clos-de-chacras.flagship_grapes: Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon and a blend

bodega-comunitaria-los-amaichas.history: It began operating in 2016 and is managed by the Indigenous Community of Amaicha del Valle, of the Diaguita Nation. It is the only Indigenous community winery in Argentina and the third in the world. It makes wine from the grapes of about 40 growers in the valleys.
highlights: First community winery in Latin America and third in the world
About 60 families work in the project
Makes wine from the grapes of 40 growers in Amaicha, Los Zazos and Colalao

bodega-dal-borgo.history: A family project in Animaná: Sergio Dal Borgo planted vineyards in 2010, and the winery has made its own wines since 2017. It has 20 ha planted, and its Almandino range takes its name from a local mineral. The winemaker is Daniel Heffner.
highlights: Almandino range, named after a local mineral
Blend of Cabernet Franc, Malbec and Tannat
Guided tours Wednesday to Sunday by reservation

bodega-dante-robino.history: Founded in 1920 on the legacy of Piedmont-born Dante Robino, it was privately owned until 2020, when it was bought by Cervecería y Maltería Quilmes, part of the AB InBev group. It makes still and sparkling wines.
highlights: Capacity to produce 11.5 million litres of wine.
bodega-dante-robino.flagship_grapes: 100% Malbec from Los Chacayes (Uco Valley); aged in French oak barrels

bodega-del-gredal.history: A family winery in northern Córdoba, in San Pedro Norte, with vineyards at about 1,000 metres altitude. It makes the Misitorco and Quishca ranges.
highlights: Misitorco Sauvignon Blanc, highlighted by Decanter
Vineyards at about 1,000 m a.s.l. in northern Córdoba

bodega-des-de-la-torre.history: The first winery in Chos Malal, in northern Neuquén, located between the Curí Leuvú and Neuquén rivers. Its Criolla de Pueblo range uses grapes from old vines, and the soil is limestone of marine origin.
highlights: First winery in the Chos Malal area
One of its bottles reached the Vatican as a gift to Pope Francis

bodega-divendres.history: A winery in Los Barriales, Junín, conceived as a meeting place around wine. It makes wine in small vessels, with capacity for 90,000 bottles a year.

bodega-domiciano.history: A family winery founded in 2005 by the Fernández family together with winemaker Rodrigo Gasparoni. It vinifies in Barrancas (Maipú) and is based in Coquimbito. It is known for harvesting before dawn to preserve the freshness of the grapes.
highlights: Night harvest: grapes are picked in the early hours, close to dawn
Vineyards in the Barrancas GI, with alluvial soils of rounded stones
bodega-domiciano.flagship_grapes: Flagship range of night-harvested varietals from Barrancas

bodega-don-celedonio.history: A winery in an adobe building with galleries on a hillside overlooking the valley, beside Ruta 68 at the entrance to Cafayate. It receives visitors.

bodega-don-eduardo.history: A winery in Colalao del Valle included in the Ruta del Vino de Altura of Tucumán. According to the official guide, it does not receive tourist visits.

bodega-don-manuel-villafane.history: A winery in El Paraíso (Maipú) created in 2008 in homage to Don Manuel Villafañe, a pioneer of colonial viticulture. It exports to Brazil, the United States, England and China, among others, and offers tours, tastings and blending workshops.
highlights: Visits with tank tastings and blending your own wine

bodega-dos-familias.history: Its main building, from 1861, operated as a wheat mill and was converted into a winery in 1894. Restored since 2002 by its current owners, in 2004 it was declared Historical, Cultural and Architectural Heritage of Luján de Cuyo.
highlights: Capacity of 962,000 litres; ferments in concrete vats and ages in an underground cellar.

bodega-el-bayeh.history: A winery in the Quebrada de Humahuaca, a member of the Asociación Bodegas de la Quebrada de Humahuaca, which in November 2025 presented its wines in Buenos Aires together with eight other Jujuy wineries.

bodega-el-cese.history: A boutique winery in Angastaco, on Ruta 40. Milagro Zamora's parents planted vines in 2006, with the first harvest in 2009; they made wine in Cafayate until 2011 and then in Angastaco. It produces about 70,000 litres a year.
highlights: Production of about 70,000 litres a year
Guided tour and tasting every day from 9 am to 5 pm

bodega-el-chanar.history: A winery in Colalao del Valle, on Ruta 40, included in the Ruta del Vino de Altura of Tucumán. It receives visitors every day.

bodega-el-molino-cachi.history: An establishment 9 km from Cachi that Welcome Argentina includes in its list of Salta wineries, categorised as accommodation.

bodega-el-transito.history: A winery in the centre of Cafayate, around the corner from Nanni, owned and run by a member of the Nanni family. It sells its wines at the winery rather than in supermarkets; its labels feature Tannat, Malbec and Cabernet.

highlights: Part of the Camino del Vino of Río Negro, on route 151

bodega-entre-tapias.history: It presents itself as the first boutique winery in Barreal, in the Calingasta Valley, at 1,650 m above sea level. It belongs to the group of wineries distinguished for the quality of their wine tourism services on the San Juan Wine Route.
highlights: Quality distinction for wine tourism services (San Juan Wine Route)
Winery in Barreal at 1,650 m a.s.l.

bodega-enzo-bianchi.history: The Uco Valley winery of Bodegas Bianchi, a family company with more than 90 years of history. In Los Chacayes it makes its icon wines, such as IV Generación, Particular and the sparkling Stradivarius.
highlights: Makes Bodegas Bianchi's icon wines in Los Chacayes.
90-minute guided tours in Spanish, English and Portuguese.

bodega-escorihuela-gascon.history: Founded in 1884 in Godoy Cruz by Spanish immigrants, with Miguel Escorihuela Gascón as its central figure. It is one of Mendoza's historic wineries; from the mid-1940s it supplied wines to Juan Perón and Eva Perón.
highlights: One of the oldest active wineries in Mendoza (1884)
Created the President's Blend for Juan and Eva Perón, according to Flaschenpost
Has a vineyard in Agrelo with a polo field among the vines

bodega-etnia.history: Its history begins with Miguel Malizia, born in Catania, who arrived in San Rafael in 1906 and built a winery with his wife Gracia Constanzo. Today it is run by their great-grandchildren in Rama Caída.
highlights: Family winery run by the fourth generation (the founder's great-grandchildren).

bodega-fabril-alto-verde.history: A Pocito winery that makes varietal and sparkling wines from its own vineyards, which the official tourism portal describes as 100% organic with national and international certification. It focuses on organic fine wines for export.
highlights: 100% organic vineyards with national and international certification (sanjuan.tur.ar)
Quality distinction for wine tourism services (San Juan Wine Route)

bodega-familia-cassone.history: A family winery in Mayor Drummond, at 950 m a.s.l., built in 1998 in the traditional Mendoza style, with high walls and pitch-pine ceilings. It uses its own vineyards, more than a hundred years old, in Luján de Cuyo and ages in French oak barrels.
highlights: Own vineyards more than a hundred years old in Luján de Cuyo.

bodega-familia-cecchin.history: Santiago Cecchin arrived from Treviso in 1910; in 1959 his sons Pedro and Jorge opened their own vineyard and winery in Russell (Maipú). Today it is run by Alberto Cecchin and is a pioneer in organic wines, certified since 2001.
highlights: Organic certification since 2001, also for Canada, the US, Japan and Europe
Makes natural, chemical-free wines in Russell, Maipú

bodega-familia-di-tommaso.history: A winery in Russell (Maipú) that has made wine since 1869, according to the South America Wine Guide. It preserves artisanal technology from the last century and is a regular stop on the Maipú bike circuit, with a restaurant.
highlights: Has produced wine since 1869; displays old artisanal winemaking equipment

bodega-familia-giaquinta.history: A family of Italian immigrants in wine since 1915. Don José Giaquinta began as a vineyard contractor in La Arboleda (Tupungato), and in 1968 the family began making wine in its own winery; since 1980 it has bottled its wines.
highlights: Four generations in winemaking since 1915
Near the winery stands the founding monolith of the Tupungato department

bodega-familia-ibarra.history: A family of grape growers since 1914 that began making its own artisanal wines in 1980. The winery is in Rama Caída, on the road to Valle Grande, and is devoted to organic wines; its restaurant also operates there.
highlights: Makes organic wines; fourth generation of the family.
Extra Brut sparkling wine, 100% Chardonnay, traditional method.

bodega-familia-mayol.history: In the early 20th century the Mayol grandparents bought their first vineyard in Tupungato and grew grapes on a small scale. Their children continued, and today the family works three estates (Montuiri, Sebastián and Pircas) with vines 40 to 70 years old.
highlights: Vines 40 to 70 years old on alluvial loam soil with limestone.
Finca Montuiri, Finca Pircas and Cuatro Primos wines.

bodega-familia-morgan.history: A boutique winery in San Rafael founded by a family with North American roots that came to the region more than 15 years ago. It makes premium wines advised by Marcelo Pelleriti; the winemaker is Jonathan Muñoz.
highlights: Reserva Malbec and Red Blend 2020 awarded medals at the Decanter World Wine Awards, with five vintages.

bodega-familia-sacavino-arrieta.history: An artisanal family winery in Los Palacios, Felipe Varela department, devoted exclusively to Torrontés Riojano. Its wine is Sumalao. It offers guided tours with tastings, meals by reservation and accommodation.

bodega-favretto.history: Ferruccio Favretto arrived in the Alto Valle around 1927, worked on irrigation canals and in 1944 planted his first vines and set up the winery in Villa Regina. Today it is run by his grandson Gustavo Favretto, trained in France, Spain and Napa.
highlights: Family company with more than 70 years of winemaking in Villa Regina
Run by the third generation, Gustavo Favretto
bodega-favretto.flagship_grapes: Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon, multi-vintage (2010, 2015, 2016, 2017), in magnum

bodega-fernando-dupont.history: The winery of agronomist Fernando Dupont in Maimará, considered the first in the Quebrada de Humahuaca, with vineyards planted from 2003. It farms 5 ha and produces about 23,000 litres a year. Its wine is Pasacana.
highlights: First winery in the Quebrada de Humahuaca, according to Wines of Argentina
Quebrada de Humahuaca GI (recognised in 2015)
Tasting with local cured meats and goat's cheese
bodega-fernando-dupont.flagship_grapes: Blend of Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah

highlights: Once Acres: Malbec from vines more than 80 years old in La Consulta.
bodega-finca-abril.flagship_grapes: 100% Malbec from La Consulta vines more than 80 years old; 18 months in new French oak

bodega-finca-cuadro-benegas.history: A winery built in 1936 by Salvador Paolucci, who from 1938 sold his wines as Paolucci e Hijos. In 1950 Gilberto Lavaque joined and it was renamed Rodas SA. Since 2012 it has had a new owner and adopted the name of the district.
highlights: Capacity of 1,200,000 litres and a bottling line of 3,500 bottles per hour.
Exports to Uruguay, Chile, Colombia and China.

bodega-finca-el-nevado.history: A family winery in San Rafael with vineyards on the north bank of the Atuel River, at the foot of Cerro Negro. It makes wines in various ranges and offers vineyard tours with tasting.
highlights: 70 hectares with drip irrigation, vertical shoot positioning and spur-pruned cordon.

bodega-finca-la-churita.history: A winery in Colalao del Valle with an old vineyard, making high-altitude wines at 1,850 m a.s.l. It is part of the Ruta del Vino de Altura of Tucumán.

bodega-finca-la-orilla.history: A small artisanal winery with a family heritage in Colalao del Valle. Its Micuna range includes a Malbec and an oak-aged blend, the latter award-winning according to the official tourism board.

bodega-finca-savina.history: Family winery in Lunlunta (Maipú) founded in 2017 by Abelardo and Ángela Savina. The wines are designed by their granddaughter, winemaker Guadalupe Savina, and the family hosts visits, tastings and a weekend restaurant.
highlights: Three generations of the Savina family working at the winery
Viejo Sabio Reserva range, partly aged in French oak
bodega-finca-savina.flagship_grapes: Malbec (2021 vintage); reserve range in limited lots of 2,000 bottles made from the best of each harvest

bodega-florio.history: Founded in 1912 by Italian immigrant Antonio Florio in Cruz de Piedra (Maipú). It specialises in fortified wines of Italian and European tradition, such as Marsala, Moscato, Port and Sherry styles; two Argentine families later joined and expanded the range.
highlights: Specialises in fortified wines: Marsala, Moscato, Port and Sherry styles
Makes styles of Italian tradition such as Gamba di Pernice and Nebbiolo

bodega-fortaleza.history: A family winery in Tucumán's Calchaquí Valleys that presents itself as the first in Argentina to sell 100% of its production online. Its ranges are Don Aldo, Julio Julián, Patriarca, Pazioca and Río Revuelto.
highlights: 100% online sales, according to the winery

bodega-funckenhausen.history: Kurt Heinlein, of German origin, looked in 2003 for a terroir for a family project honouring his Funcke ancestors. He bought 350 hectares in 25 de Mayo, San Rafael, and in 2005 planted the first 20 with Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah.
highlights: Vineyard at 850 m, among the highest in San Rafael according to South America Wine Guide.
Launched a premium wine in a 1-litre format.
bodega-funckenhausen.flagship_grapes: Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon from micro-plots

bodega-garbin-estate.history: A family project born in 1978 in the city of San Rafael, now focused on bottling and developing wine brands. It exports to more than twenty countries in the Americas, Europe and Asia.

bodega-gennari.history: A family winery in General Fernández Oro, on provincial route 65, that produces wine and dried fruit.

bodega-gimenez-riili.history: The Giménez Riili family has worked the land and made wine since 1920. Today the boutique winery in Los Chacayes is run by the fourth generation, Belén and Federico, and also has a restaurant and guesthouse.
highlights: Family winery in its fourth generation.
Guesthouse with 8 themed rooms and a suite at the winery.
Restaurant with tasting menus by chef Sebastián Juez.

bodega-goyenechea.history: Brothers Santiago and Narciso Goyenechea, Spanish immigrants, opened a wine business in Buenos Aires in 1868. They later bought a vineyard in Villa Atuel and built a village with a school and chapel around the winery. It is run by the third, fourth and fifth generations.
highlights: It was part of the first Council of the San Rafael DOC and exported the first wine bearing that DOC.
It preserves the original 1905 building, chapel and main house on the La Vasconia estate.

bodega-haarth.history: The history of the site begins in 1923, when an Italian family planted the first vines in Colonia López, Villa Atuel. In 2011 it was bought by its current owners, of Canadian farming background, who achieved the area's first organic certification for vineyard and winery.
highlights: First organic certification of vineyards and winery in the area (2011).
Inn with rooms and a pool at the winery.

bodega-hacienda-del-plata.history: A boutique family winery founded in 1999 in Luján de Cuyo. It farms two vineyards of its own: 4.5 hectares in Chacras de Coria and 8 in Carrodilla.

bodega-hagmann.history: A family winery in the city of San Juan, 5 km from Plaza 25 de Mayo, that has made wines and mistelle since 1947. It offers tastings and is part of the provincial Wine Route.
highlights: Makes mistelle as well as wines
Recipient of provincial wine tourism funding (2023)

bodega-haras-san-jose.history: An artisanal winery in Villa Unión, in the Bermejo valley. It offers guided tours with tastings of wines and local foods, and sells its products.

bodega-hinojosa.history: In 1940 Silvestre Hinojosa bought the Dumit family's winery in Tunuyán, beginning the winemaking history of the family, which still runs it. It is an urban winery with vineyards between 1,000 and 1,200 m irrigated with snowmelt.
highlights: Urban winery in the city of Tunuyán, owned by the same family since 1940.
Visit with a tasting of three wines in the Sala Victoria.

bodega-iaccarini.history: Founded in 1903 by Neapolitan immigrant Pascual Iaccarini, it was the first winery in the Las Paredes district. After years closed, the Méndez Collado family revived it in 2009; it was later sold again and now seeks to export premium wines.
highlights: Cavas Don Nicasio, Bodega Iaccarini and Vía Blanca ranges.
Reports a presence in more than 16 countries.

bodega-isasmendi.history: Founded in 2005 by Ricardo Isasmendi and Sylvie Bonnal in an old house-winery in Cachi built in the 20th century by a Norwegian doctor. It farms 3 ha at 2,500 m a.s.l. and makes about 12,000 bottles a year through micro-vinifications.
highlights: 400 kg micro-vinifications with manual pump-overs
Four-course lunch by advance reservation
About 12,000 bottles a year

bodega-iudica.history: Iúdica Vinos began in 1983 growing grapes in San Roque (Maipú), and in 2008 it bought a winery with 19th-century foundations, which it restored. Its owners and winemakers guide the visits with tasting.
highlights: Winery with 19th-century foundations, restored after its purchase in 2008

bodega-jorge-rubio.history: A family winery founded in 2003 by winemaker Jorge Alberto Rubio on the outskirts of General Alvear. It produces about 1.4 million litres a year, with more than 35 labels including still wines, sparkling wines and spirits.
highlights: Cellar with more than 700 French and American oak barrels.
Makes traditional-method sparkling wines and spirits distilled in old French alembic stills.
bodega-jorge-rubio.flagship_grapes: Emblematic range of reds with 12 months in oak and a leather label

bodega-josefa-rodo-finca-el-carmen.history: The Miralpeix family estate on Ruta 40, between Angastaco and Molinos, with the Josefa Rodó winery. It has agricultural, archaeological and sacred art museums, a chapel from 1780, a restaurant, hotel and cabins.
highlights: Chapel from 1780 on the estate
Agricultural, archaeological and sacred art museums

bodega-kindgard.history: A winery with vineyards and wine tourism in Purmamarca, in an area above 2,300 m a.s.l. It offers vineyard and cellar tours, tastings, a regional cuisine restaurant and cabins facing the Cerro de los Siete Colores. Its labels are Copleras, Sacha Tigre and Purma.
highlights: Boutique cabins facing the Cerro de los Siete Colores
Tasting of three labels with local cheeses and preserves
Quebrada de Humahuaca GI (recognised in 2015)

bodega-la-abeja.history: The first winery in San Rafael, built by Frenchman Rodolfo Iselín, founder of the city, who called it La Juanita. It passed to the Schlieper family and then to the Ripas, who restored it in 2004 to make wine and open it to tourism.
highlights: Preserves original machinery from 1885 brought from France.
Located in the urban centre of San Rafael.

bodega-la-azul.history: Francisco Hinojosa's family has grown grapes at the foot of the Cordón del Plata for generations; in 2003 it created La Azul, a small family winery. Since 2011 it has had a restaurant with mountain views.
highlights: Small family winery at the foot of the Cordón del Plata, Tupungato.
Restaurant open since 2011 and a guesthouse on the estate.

bodega-la-baguala.history: A family project in Barreal, in the Calingasta Valley, that makes natural mountain wines by artisanal methods. It offers guided tours with tasting, by advance reservation.
highlights: Artisanally made natural mountain wines
Recipient of provincial wine tourism funding (2023)

bodega-la-blanqueada.history: A family project in Las Flores, Buenos Aires province, by a family with four generations in the area. It makes artisanal wines, including a Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon blend, and displays old winemaking tools brought from Italy.
highlights: Gallery of old winemaking tools brought from Italy

bodega-la-ejemplar.history: A winery in 9 de Julio, in the Tulum Valley, on National Route 20. It offers guided tours of the vineyard and winery with tasting, by reservation, and cabin accommodation.
highlights: Guided tours with tasting every day, by reservation
Cabin accommodation

bodega-la-fortuna.history: An artisanal winery and wine shop in Barreal, Calingasta Valley. It offers guided tours with tasting and an experience with a tasting of four labels and lunch, by advance reservation.
highlights: Wine experience with a tasting of four labels and lunch
Recipient of provincial wine tourism funding (2023)

bodega-la-indomita-municipal-de-fiambala.history: A municipal winery in Fiambalá that started with five tanks in Medanitos and within two years moved from producing must to making wine. In 2023 it presented La Indómita red, made from Fiambalá grapes, and announced an expansion plan to 1.1 million litres.
bodega-la-indomita-municipal-de-fiambala.flagship_grapes: Red from Fiambalá grapes; 8 months in barrel

bodega-la-mansa.history: Gastón Bonoldi settled in Cuadro Bombal, San Rafael, in 2001 and developed organically managed vineyards; the winery, named after his daughters' mare, opened about ten years later. It exports to Brazil, Paraguay and China.
highlights: Has its own shops in Iguazú, Ciudad del Este and São Paulo.

bodega-la-rural.history: Felipe Rutini founded Bodega La Rural in 1885 in Coquimbito (Maipú). In 1924 it was the first to plant vineyards in the Uco Valley. Today it makes wine in Tupungato under the Rutini Wines brand, and its Wine Museum operates in Coquimbito.
highlights: First winery to plant vineyards in the Uco Valley (1924)
Wine Museum with more than 4,500 pieces in Felipe Rutini's house

bodega-la-vigilia.history: A Los Chacayes winery that uses grapes from its own estate, fermenting in amphorae, steel tanks and cement vats, with ageing in French oak. It has the ROPE restaurant.
highlights: Fermentation in amphorae, steel and cement; ageing in French oak.
ROPE restaurant serving lunch, sunset and dinner.

bodega-labiano.history: A family winery in Rama Caída, San Rafael, known for its 'Wine Fountain' open to visitors.

bodega-las-hijas.history: A vineyard in Altamira, Mercedes district, planted on certified organic land where the company Planto also operates. It grows Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Marselan.
highlights: Vineyard on certified organic land

bodega-las-marianas-finca-camunas.history: An old winery in La Rinconada, Pocito, at the foot of the Sierra Chica de Zonda and at 750 m altitude. The official tourism portal credits it with more than 100 years of history; it makes wines and sparkling wines in limited lots.
highlights: Quality distinction for wine tourism services (San Juan Wine Route)
Makes wines and sparkling wines in limited lots

bodega-laureano-gomez.history: It began in 2010 as a 'Garage Winery', where the first four vintages were made, by winemakers with more than 20 years at Trapiche and Salentein. In 2014 the family built its own boutique winery in Tunuyán, which produces about 70,000 bottles a year.
highlights: Started as a garage winery; own winery built by the family in 2014.
Barrel and tank tastings with the family; disgorgement of the Rosé de Malbec sparkling wine.

bodega-lavaque.history: Winery of the Lavaque family, of Lebanese origin and with winemaking roots in Cafayate. Gilberto Lavaque established vineyards in San Rafael and his son Rodolfo took it to the national and international stage; from 1990 it adopted new technologies.
highlights: Family tradition begun in Cafayate (Salta) in 1870, according to Mendoza Travel.
Own vineyards in Cañada Seca, Barrancas del Atuel and Finca Santa Luisa (Mendoza Travel).

bodega-lavaque-2.history: The winery of a family of Syrian-Lebanese origin with five generations of winemakers, now run by Francisco Lavaque at Finca El Recreo, south of Cafayate. It moved from mass-market wines to a boutique model, with organic and regenerative practices, and planted the high-altitude Vallisto vineyard.
highlights: Torrontés from vines more than 130 years old
50 ha Vallisto vineyard with Diaguita terraces
Hotel Finca El Recreo, reopened in 2023 with 12 rooms

bodega-los-haroldos.history: Haroldo Santos Falasco began in 1939 delivering wine by bicycle in Chacabuco, Buenos Aires. His family later built the winery in San Martín, which Jorge Falasco named Los Haroldos. Today it is run by the fourth generation and exports to 42 countries.
highlights: In 2023 it joined wine tourism as Mendoza's 205th winery.
Produces more than 60 million litres, according to Diario Uno.

bodega-los-zazos.history: A winery in Los Zazos, near Amaicha del Valle, included in the Ruta del Vino de Altura of Tucumán. According to the official guide, it does not receive tourist visits.

bodega-maelca.history: An artisanal winery in Alto Carrizal, in Famatina. It offers estate tours, food, accommodation and sales, according to the official list of tourist wineries of La Rioja.

bodega-marale-wines.history: A winery in Media Agua, Sarmiento department, that combines winemaking with its own hotel and restaurant. It is part of the San Juan Wine Route.
highlights: Offers accommodation and dining at the winery
Recipient of provincial wine tourism funding (2023)

bodega-mauricio-lorca.history: Enrique Foster and winemaker Mauricio Lorca built the winery in Perdriel where, since 2008, they have made the Foster and Lorca brands. Lorca presents himself as a pioneer of unoaked premium wines and works with grapes from Luján de Cuyo, the Uco Valley and eastern Mendoza.

bodega-melipal.history: Founded in 2002 by Ignacio Aristi in Agrelo, it was bought by Achaval Ferrer in 2019. It has two vineyards: 60 hectares next to the winery and 25 hectares of Malbec planted in the 1920s.
highlights: 25-hectare Malbec vineyard planted in the 1920s.

bodega-merced-del-estero.history: A boutique family winery at the far western end of the Tulum Valley, in Marquesado. The family has worked the 14 ha estate since 1897, and visits are guided by the owners themselves. It was one of the first three certified under the Wine Tourism Sustainability Self-Assessment Guide.
highlights: Estate worked by the family since 1897
Among the first three certified in wine tourism sustainability
Mil Vientos range, barrel-aged (Malbec; Cabernet Sauvignon-Cabernet Franc)

bodega-miraluna.history: A project of the Urtasun family in Cachi, begun in 2004 as a tourist cabin complex to which vineyards and a winery were later added. It has a 3 ha estate at about 2,600 m a.s.l., at the foot of the Nevado de Cachi. The vineyards and winemaking are directed by Ukrainian Sergei Marusik.
highlights: Wines of up to 16% alcohol
Production of up to 25,000 bottles a year
Boutique cabins among the vineyards

bodega-montequieto.history: Matilde Pereda and Agustín Casabal bought an estate in Agrelo in 2000 and founded Monte Quieto; they later added estates in Ugarteche and Vista Flores. From the outset they chose Cabernet Franc as the main emblem of their wines.
highlights: Alegre Gran Corte marked 15 years with the 2020 edition.
bodega-montequieto.flagship_grapes: Blend of Cabernet Franc (43%), Malbec (35%) and Syrah (22%) from its three vineyards; 12 months in second-use barrels (2020 vintage)

bodega-monteviejo.history: A Vista Flores winery that is part of the Clos de los Siete project. Construction began in early 2001 and the first harvest was in 2002; it operates by gravity, without pumps, over 8,500 m².
highlights: Member of Clos de los Siete in Vista Flores.
Gravity-flow winery; first harvest in 2002.

bodega-morchio-meglioli.history: A winery in San Martín, in the Tulum Valley, where El Altillo wines are made. It offers tours of the winery and vineyards with a tasting of varietals, by advance reservation.
highlights: Makes the El Altillo brand
Winery and vineyard visit with a tasting of varietals

bodega-municipal-de-hualfin.history: Founded in 2011, it presents itself as the first municipal winery in Latin America. It was created so that Hualfín's small growers would not depend on wineries in Cafayate or Santa María. It buys grapes from 15 to 20 local growers and has no vineyards of its own.
highlights: First municipal winery in Latin America, according to the source
Capacity of 320,000 litres and a cellar for 200 barrels
Makes Torrontés, Malbec and an organic range

bodega-murville.history: Sicilian Rafael Salafia bought an estate in Las Paredes in 1937 and in 1945 built the winery, devoted to bulk wine. He dreamed of sparkling wines, which his grandchildren realised in the 1990s with the Murville brand.
highlights: First Argentine winery to make natural frizzante wines (Il Segreto).
Organic wine certification since 2003 and ISO 9001 in 2007.
bodega-murville.flagship_grapes: Malbec 60%, Cabernet Sauvignon 20%, Cabernet Franc 20%; 24 months in American oak

bodega-nanni.history: A family winery founded in 1897, one block from the main square of Cafayate, now in the hands of the fourth generation of the Nanni family. It makes certified organic wines and has a restaurant in its courtyard.
highlights: Fourth generation of the Nanni family
Certified organic wines
Retoño restaurant in the courtyard

bodega-navarro-correas.history: The Correas family has planted vines in Mendoza since 1798, when Juan de Dios Correas did so. For a century it sold grapes and wine to others, until in 1974 Edmundo Navarro Correas began bottling under his own name. It has a cellar in Godoy Cruz and an estate in Agrelo.
highlights: Family origins in 1798, with Juan de Dios Correas
bodega-navarro-correas.flagship_grapes: Blend of 82% Malbec and 18% Cabernet Sauvignon, 18 months in French oak and a further 12 months of ageing

bodega-nieto-senetiner.history: Its history begins in 1888, when Italian immigrants founded the winery and planted vineyards in Vistalba. In 1969 it was bought by the Nieto Senetiner family, and since 1998 it has belonged to the Molinos Río de la Plata group.
highlights: Part of the Luján de Cuyo DOC.

bodega-nueva-corinema.history: An experimental vineyard of about 1,400 vines in Altamira, Mercedes, set in the ruins of the Corinema brick and tile factory, with vaulted tunnels, kilns and a 25-metre chimney inaugurated in 1947.
highlights: Preserves one of the country's two Hoffmann continuous kilns
Experimental vineyard with Malbec, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Marselan, among others

bodega-obra-don-bosco.history: The Salesians arrived in Rodeo del Medio in 1898, and in 1901 they began classes in viticulture and oenology and the experimental winery. In 1965 the school gave rise to the first faculty of oenology in Latin America. It has a cellar from 1880 and a modern winery from 2007.
highlights: First faculty of oenology in Latin America (1965)
The only winery with wine-tower architecture in Latin America, according to the tourism board
Cellar from 1880 and a modern winery opened in 2007
bodega-obra-don-bosco.flagship_grapes: Varietal Lambrusco Maestri made by the Don Bosco Faculty of Oenology

bodega-pecne-te.history: Swiss Urs Gmür bought undeveloped land in Alto Verde, San Martín, in 2006 and planted vines, walnut trees and plum trees. In 2008 other Swiss investors joined, and in 2018 they acquired a boutique winery to vinify.
highlights: In addition to wines, it produces olive oils and spirits.
