bodega-piattelli.history: Piattelli Vineyards is the project of the Malinski couple, who opened their first winery in Agrelo and in late 2008 bought estates in Cafayate, Salta. In Agrelo it offers comparisons of wines from both regions.

bodega-piattelli-2.history: The winery of Americans Jon and Arlene Malinski, with estates in Mendoza and Cafayate. In Cafayate it operates opposite the Piattelli Wine Resort, with twenty casitas, a spa and restaurants. Its winemaker is Valeria Antolín.
highlights: Adults-only wine resort with 20 casitas and a spa
Daily visits with or without tasting

bodega-piedra-negra.history: The François Lurton group's winery in Los Chacayes. After searching several regions of Argentina, Lurton planted on high, semi-desert land in the Uco Valley and built the winery at the centre of 200 ha of virgin land, with environmentally respectful viticulture.
highlights: Poor gravel soils, compared by the winery to those of Pessac-Léognan.
A pioneer in Los Chacayes, on a 200 ha estate.
Organic philosophy, according to the winery.

bodega-pulmary.history: Family winery producing small quantities of organic wine. The family began growing grapes in 1998 in its Medrano vineyard and soon afterwards started making wine; in Chacras de Coria it uses small concrete vats and an underground cellar.
highlights: Own vineyard on the banks of the Tunuyán River, in Medrano (Mendoza), according to the winery.

bodega-puna.history: A Cachi winery with 36 ha planted on two sites, Cachi (2,600 m a.s.l.) and La Poma, producing about 420,000 bottles a year. It offers free tours, tastings and a restaurant with a pairing menu.
highlights: Vineyards in La Poma, above 3,200 m a.s.l.
Four-course pairing menu by reservation
Works nine varieties, from Malbec to Chardonnay

bodega-putruele.history: A family winery in Dos Acequias, San Martín, that reports more than half a century of experience and operates as Putruele Hnos. It offers guided tours with tasting and pairing, and multi-course lunches under the oldest pergola on the estate.
highlights: Three-course paired lunch, Thursday to Sunday
More than half a century of experience, according to the winery

bodega-quietud.history: A winery in Santa Rosa, La Pampa, formed in 2009, that makes wine from grapes grown at the Casa de Piedra Experimental Farm, such as Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc and Malbec.
highlights: Medals and diplomas in international competitions, according to the La Pampa wine route

bodega-quimera.history: According to its tourism listing, it presents itself as a 'House of Blends' and offers tastings, tours and a restaurant in Agrelo.

bodega-rj-vinedos.history: Raúl Jofré founded RJ Viñedos in 1998 to revive his family's winegrowing tradition and share it with his four daughters. It operates in a restored 1940 winery in Perdriel and exports about 80% of its production.
highlights: Joffré e Hijas Gran Malbec: 91 points in Descorchados 2014, according to the winery.

bodega-raffy-familia-zanchetta.history: A small-scale family winery in Gualtallary, at about 1,300 m, with an organic vineyard. For more than 15 years it has incorporated sound therapy and bioenergy into its vineyard work.
highlights: Botella 333 Gran Malbec: 96 points from Andreas Larsson (Tasted).
Organic vineyard in Gualtallary, with sound therapy applied to the vines.

bodega-red-slopes.history: The winery of a family of home winemakers on the road to Los Zazos, in Amaicha del Valle. In addition to wines, it offers presentations on native medicinal plants.

bodega-renacer.history: Founded in 2003 by Chilean businessman Patricio Reich to make premium Malbec-based wines, in a Tuscan-inspired building in Perdriel. In December 2024 it passed to the Brazilian group Miolo.
highlights: Gold at Best Of Mendoza's Wine Tourism 2016, Small Wineries category.
Member of the DOC Luján de Cuyo.
bodega-renacer.flagship_grapes: Malbec from selected blocks in Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley; extended ageing in French oak barrels and in bottle

bodega-romano-pin.history: A winery in La Cañada, Albardón, that makes wine from grapes grown on its own estate. It has underground cellars, a panoramic viewpoint and cabins for overnight stays, and is part of the San Juan Wine Route.
highlights: Estate varieties: Malbec, Tannat, Muscat, Torrontés and Sauvignon Blanc
Quality distinction for wine tourism services (San Juan Wine Route)
Underground cellars and cabin accommodation

bodega-ruca-malen.history: Founded in late 1998 by Jean Pierre Thibaud and Jacques Louis de Montalembert, both with long careers at Chandon, it received its first harvest in 1999 under the name Bodega Bacchus. It has been certified organic since 2020.
highlights: Certified organic winery since 2020.

bodega-rio-de-arena.history: A rural estancia in El Bañado, on Ruta 40, combining a winery, traditional cuisine and accommodation. It also breeds llamas and Peruvian horses.

bodega-saldungaray.history: A winery in the tourist town of Saldungaray, Tornquist district, regarded as a pioneer of winemaking in the Buenos Aires hills. It has 20 hectares with eight varieties and makes young wines and sparkling wines.
highlights: A wine pioneer in the hills of southern Buenos Aires province
Guided tours Thursday to Sunday year-round

bodega-san-huberto.history: A winery of Italian origin founded in 1921 in Vistalba, with an old building, large concrete vats and an underground cellar. The company also has production in the Aminga valley (La Rioja) and in Huailai, China.

bodega-san-javier-noble-de-san-javier.history: Winemaker Nicolás Jascalevich started the project in 2001 in San Javier, Traslasierra, aiming to revive the area's lost winemaking tradition. It grows Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon and Tannat organically and also has an inn among the vineyards.
highlights: Organic farming, according to Decanter
Free guided tours with tasting and a cheese-and-charcuterie platter

bodega-san-polo.history: A La Consulta winery with 180 ha of vineyards in San Carlos, between 1,000 and 1,200 m, on stony alluvial soils irrigated with snowmelt.
highlights: 180 ha in San Carlos with Malbec, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir, Tempranillo and white varieties.

bodega-santa-julia.history: A Zuccardi family project in Maipú: Alberto 'Tito' Zuccardi planted his first vineyard in 1963 to test an irrigation system. The brand is named after Julia Zuccardi, who runs it today. It was the first winery with a visitor centre and its own restaurant.
highlights: More than 150 ha of certified organic vineyards in Maipú
First Argentine winery to open a visitor centre with its own restaurant, according to Turismo
Has the Zuelo olive oil mill and the Pan y Oliva restaurant
bodega-santa-julia.flagship_grapes: Blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Malbec with a little Syrah, Uco Valley

bodega-santa-maria-de-la-vid.history: A project of the Prelature of Cafayate begun in 1992 in La Soledad, 3 km from Santa María. It planted 40 ha of vines on formerly desert land and produces about 60,000 bottles a year. Its speciality is Barbera.
highlights: Winery of the Prelature of Cafayate, also labelled Bodega Prelatura
Makes Torrontés, Syrah, Malbec and Barbera

bodega-simonassi-lyon.history: It was founded in 1983 on the initiative of the married couple Jorge Simonassi Lyon and Silvia Romano. Today it is run by Silvia and her daughters Florencia and Renata, with production of about 60,000 bottles and a transition towards regenerative agriculture.
highlights: Preserves an old Malbec vineyard from 1922.
Labels designed in part by Florencia, a graphic designer.

bodega-sin-fin.history: A family company founded in 1975 by Carlos Caselles to grow grapes in Rodeo del Medio (Maipú). Over time it added premium winemaking and today receives visitors with tastings and lunches.
highlights: Its first vineyard, El Descanso, has Malbec, Cabernet and Bonarda
bodega-sin-fin.flagship_grapes: Malbec and blends with 18 months in barrel

bodega-solo-contigo.history: Canadians Terry and Noel Neelands, art collectors, bought an estate in Los Chacayes in 2009 and in 2014 began building their winery with the Bórmida y Yanzón studio. The building includes an art gallery with an inverted pyramid.
highlights: 120,000-litre winery designed by Bórmida y Yanzón.
Art gallery with an inverted pyramid inside the building.
Develado range, with minimal-intervention wines and indigenous yeasts.
bodega-solo-contigo.flagship_grapes: Limited-release red (1,500 bottles); the winery does not disclose grapes or ageing

bodega-stocco-de-viani.history: Founded in 1950 by brothers Carlos and Francisco Stocco, sons of Italian immigrants, in Maipú. They built the winery in the late 1950s; the third generation took over in 2002, and since 2010 it has bottled its own brands.
highlights: 40 ha of its own vineyards in Maipú
Open to wine tourism since 2012, on the Maipú Wine Route

bodega-suter.history: Founded in San Rafael by Swiss Otto Rodolfo Suter, who arrived in 1897 with his wife Ana to grow vines as his parents had. It is one of the country's historic brands, with more than 100 harvests.
highlights: Sells about 11 million litres a year across all its ranges.
Its Etiqueta Marrón is considered a classic.

bodega-septima.history: Séptima is the seventh project of the Spanish group Raventós Codorníu and celebrated 25 years in 2026. It is located in Agrelo, at 1,050 m a.s.l., surrounded by the 150-hectare Finca Emblema. The building, by Bórmida & Yanzón, uses the pirca dry-stone technique with stones from the Mendoza River.
highlights: Belongs to the Codorníu group (Codorniu Argentina), according to iProfesional (2023).
Its winery in Agrelo, Luján de Cuyo, covers 5,500 m² (Sitio Andino, 2015).
bodega-septima.flagship_grapes: Malbec from the winery's best lot, 24 months in new French oak barrels and 36 months in bottle

bodega-tempus-alba.history: A winery in Coquimbito (Maipú) founded by the Biondolillo family, now run by its fifth generation. Its name means 'Time of Dawn'. It developed its own Malbec clone project and offers a self-guided tour and a restaurant.
highlights: VERO Malbec: 93 points from Tim Atkin
Best Of Wine Tourism: first prize in Wine Tourism Experiences
Malbec clone project developed by the family

bodega-terra-lombarda.history: An old winery in Rama Caída, San Rafael, restored by a family as a home, tourism venue and artisanal winery. It produces around 5,000 bottles a year.

bodega-tierra-del-huarpe.history: A Chimbas winery created in 2001 by a partnership of eight San Juan farmers, who first rented the facility and later bought it. It has capacity for almost 10 million litres and processes 7 to 9 million kilos of grapes a year (2017).
highlights: Capacity of close to 10 million litres (Diario de Cuyo, 2017)

bodega-tierras-altas.history: Brothers Vicente, Daniel and Rodolfo Vargas Arizu, third generation of a family linked to wine since Leoncio Arizu in 1890, built Tierras Altas in 1999. Today part of the fourth generation also works on the project.
highlights: Century-old winery of the Vargas Arizu family in Luján de Cuyo, according to its official website.

bodega-tornaghi.history: César Tornaghi, an Italian immigrant who worked at the first winery in San Rafael, bought land in the city centre in 1893 for his own project. Today it is run by the fifth generation of the family.
highlights: Preserves its historic underground cellar, open to visitors.

bodega-tukma.history: Fernando and Luis Maurette and Raúl Noceti bought the Tolombón estate in 2003, formerly the weekend home of the Michel Torino family. It has 35 ha there and vineyards in Huacalera and Angastaco; it produces about 220,000 bottles a year, mainly Malbec and Torrontés.
highlights: The name recalls a Diaguita chief
Hotel Altalaluna, in an 1892 house among the vineyards
Vineyards also in Huacalera (Jujuy) and Angastaco

bodega-tupun.history: The winery of the Pelegrina family, of Spanish immigrant origin, in Tupungato winemaking since 1950. It has more than 250 ha of vineyards and makes the Tupun, Vulcano and Cuño brands.
highlights: Tupun Malbec 2008: 90 points from Robert Parker, according to the winery's profile.

bodega-valle-de-choromoro.history: A winery in El Simbolar, Trancas department, outside the Calchaquí Valleys. It is listed on the Ruta del Vino de Altura of Tucumán among those that do not receive visitors.

bodega-valle-de-la-puerta.history: A winery in Vichigasta, Chilecito, between the Famatina and Velasco ranges, that produces wines and olive oil from its estates. It is known for its reds, including Malbec and Bonarda. Its symbol is the puma.
highlights: Produces extra virgin olive oil from Arbequina, Picual, Barnea and Frantoio
Guided tours Monday to Saturday and bike rides through vineyards and olive groves

bodega-veralma.history: A winery in Tinogasta department, Catamarca, included in the alternative wine route of northern Argentina promoted by the national tourism board.

bodega-viarago.history: An artisanal producer in Traslasierra with a sales room in Villa de las Rosas, making Malbec.

bodega-villa-borjas.history: It was born during the 2001 crisis, when mechanical engineer Pancho Bustos and co-workers from a factory began vinifying grapes that were going to be discarded: the first 12 litres were made in a demijohn. Today it produces about 20,000 bottles and mainly receives tourists.
highlights: Reds from Cabernet Franc, Tannat, Malbec, Carmenère and Tempranillo
Production of approximately 20,000 bottles (2022)

bodega-vinorum-finca-altieri.history: The Altieri family bought a winery built in 1930 in Perdriel in 1998 and converted it into a boutique winery for premium wines. It houses the Museum of Wine Culture, with more than 3,000 pieces.
highlights: El Victorio Altieri Gran Reserva Malbec 2023: 96 points in Descorchados 2026.
Sustainability certification, according to its tourism listing.

bodega-vinos-de-aicuna.history: An artisanal winery founded by grape growers from the village of Aicuña, Felipe Varela department, and still growing. It receives visitors with tastings and sells its wines.

bodega-vistalba.history: Carlos Pulenta, third generation of a winemaking family, founded Bodega Vistalba in 2003 on a family estate. The building works by gravity flow, without pumps. Alejandro Bulgheroni has been involved since 2009, and the winery is now managed by Paula Pulenta, of the fourth generation.
highlights: Member of the DOC Luján de Cuyo.
bodega-vistalba.flagship_grapes: Malbec blend with around 10% Cabernet Sauvignon

bodega-vistandes.history: A boutique winery opened in 2006 in Cruz de Piedra (Maipú) by a Mendoza family with a long farming history. It uses its own grapes from Maipú and the Famatina Valley (La Rioja) and has a restaurant and event halls.
highlights: Own vineyards in Maipú and in Chilecito, La Rioja, at 1,050 m a.s.l.
300 productive hectares of its own, according to the winery

bodega-vittorio-longo.history: A winery in Tinogasta, Catamarca, located in the Los Robledos neighbourhood, which appears in Welcome Argentina's list of Catamarca wineries.

bodega-wapisa.history: A winery in San Javier, about 30 km from Viedma in the lower Río Negro valley, known for ageing wines on the seabed, at 10–16 m depth in the Gulf of San Matías. Wapisa is the brand of the former Lapeyrade winery, bought by Fincas Patagónicas (Tapiz).
highlights: Ages wine in an underwater cellar off Las Grutas
Pinot Noir, Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon and Sauvignon Blanc

bodega-zolo.history: Zolo belongs to Fincas Patagónicas, of the Ortiz family, owner since 2003 and also of Tapiz and Wapisa. It is the group's only winery open to tourism. It is run by Patricia Ortiz, former president of Bodegas de Argentina.

bodega-de-aminga.history: An industrial winery in Aminga, Castro Barros department, about 80 km from the city of La Rioja. It offers guided tours, tastings and a sales room. Its social media brand is Febrero Riojano.
highlights: Visits Tuesday to Sunday, 10 am to 2 pm

bodega-del-desierto.history: A winery in 25 de Mayo, La Pampa, in the Alto Valle del Río Colorado, whose first vineyards were planted in 2001, with a second phase two years later. It totals 140 hectares and makes the Desierto25, Desierto Pampa and Pampa Mía ranges.
highlights: Vineyard in the La Pampa desert, beside the Colorado River
Mía Blanc de Blancs and Blanc de Noirs sparkling wines

bodega-y-vinedos-ansilta.history: A winery with its own vineyards in Ullum, on Provincial Route 60, offering free tours and tastings Monday to Saturday. It is part of the San Juan Wine Route.
highlights: Free tour and tasting Monday to Saturday

bodega-y-vinedos-argus.history: A boutique winery in Santa Lucía run by its owners, making fine wines from its own vineyards in the Tulum Valley. It receives visitors and is part of the San Juan Wine Route.
highlights: Boutique winery run by its owners
Recipient of provincial wine tourism funding (2023)

bodega-ultima-frontera.history: Small, family-run artisanal winery in Las Paredes, San Rafael, housed in a century-old building remodelled over the last decade. It has one hectare of organic vineyard with Petit Verdot, Cabernet Franc and Bonarda.
highlights: Family-run artisanal winery in San Rafael with more than a century of history, according to its website

bodegas-borbore.history: A family company in La Puntilla, San Martín, with a long history in San Juan winemaking. It makes fine wines at different levels for the domestic and export markets, with more than 400 ha of its own vineyards and a 4 ha industrial plant open to visitors.
highlights: More than 400 ha of its own vineyards (sanjuan.tur.ar)
Quality distinction for wine tourism services (San Juan Wine Route)

bodegas-crotta.history: José Eduardo Crotta arrived alone from Lombardy in 1919, at the age of 14. In the 1930s, with his Austrian wife Wilhelmina Ritz, he built his winery in Palmira, San Martín. Today his grandchildren carry it on, and it is known for its fortified wines.
highlights: Makes fortified wines: Moscato, Port and Marsala styles, and mistelles.

bodegas-etchart.history: One of the oldest and most important wineries in Cafayate, with a century-long history in the Calchaquí Valleys. In 1973 Arnaldo Etchart promoted the first Serenata a Cafayate. It is now linked to the Pernod Ricard group.
highlights: Origin of the first Serenata a Cafayate (1973)
Makes a late-harvest Torrontés

bodegas-san-huberto.history: A company with wineries in Vistalba (Mendoza) and in the Aminga valley (La Rioja), at the foot of Cerro Velasco, as well as a unit in China. It uses grapes from its own vineyards and exports to Australia, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom.
highlights: Exports to Australia, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom

bodegas-del-carmen.history: A winery in Villa Corral, in Calingasta, at the foot of the Precordillera and at about 1,500 m altitude, which planted its first vine in 2008. It offers guided tours of the vineyards and winery with a tasting of high-altitude wines.
highlights: First vine planted in 2008, according to the winery
Vineyard at about 1,500 m facing the Cordillera Frontal

bodegas-y-vinedos-casa-montes.history: Founded in 1992 by San Juan businessman Francisco Salvador Montes, who bought 176 ha in Pozo de los Algarrobos, Caucete, 156 of them under vine. It is run by his son Francisco Baltazar Montes. Since 2025 it has been going through a financial crisis, although in January 2026 it was still operating.
highlights: Ampakama, Fuego Negro and Baltazar brands
Capacity of 3 million litres (Tiempo de San Juan, 2026)

bodegas-y-vinedos-huanacache.history: It was founded in 2002 as Bodega Don Doménico in Huanacache, Sarmiento department, at about 606 m altitude. In late 2020 Grupo Colonia Express took control, expanded capacity and steered the project toward sustainable viticulture. Its Tecta, Chis and Cher ranges pay homage to Huarpe culture.
highlights: Cher: Malbec and Cabernet Franc blend with 12 months in French oak
Vineyards in conversion to organic certification (2021)
Solar panels for energy self-sufficiency

bodegas-y-vinedos-santos-carelli.history: In 1943 Santos J. Carelli bought a winery in La Reducción, Rivadavia, whose main hall dated from 1890, and planted vines. His son Enrique expanded it, and today the fourth generation continues with its own vineyards and winemaking.
highlights: Organic certification (LETIS) and Bodegas de Argentina sustainable winegrowing certification.
Estates in Rivadavia, San Martín and Junín.

borderio.history: A venture of Rosario businesswoman Verónica Irazoqui in Victoria, Entre Ríos, on a 50-hectare property with 12 hectares planted with various grape varieties.

bressia-bodega.history: Winemaker Walter Bressia started a 'family wines' venture with his family in 2001. He began by making wine at a friend's winery until he built his own in Agrelo.
highlights: Part of the Luján de Cuyo DOC.
bressia-bodega.flagship_grapes: Blend of Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah

cabernet-de-los-andes.history: The winery of Carlos Arizu, of a Mendoza winemaking family, on the La Retama estate, 6 km from Fiambalá. He took over the small Tizac winery and renamed it; since 2002 it has made organic wines. Its best-known wine, Plenilunio, is harvested under a full moon.
highlights: Organic wines since 2002
Plenilunio harvest festival in early April, by torchlight
Vineyards at up to 1,790–1,900 m a.s.l.
cabernet-de-los-andes.flagship_grapes: Red harvested at night under a full moon (grapes not specified)

calivista-wines.history: American David Kalainoff, raised on an Iowa farm, cleared and planted an old peach orchard near Tunuyán in 2006. The vineyard has been certified organic since the 2021 harvest.
highlights: Vineyard certified organic since the March 2021 harvest.
Guest house in the vineyard (three bedrooms).

casa-araujo.history: A San Rafael winery founded by Carlos Araujo, with vineyards irrigated by the Atuel River and certified organic production. It makes mainly reds (Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Tempranillo) and some whites.
highlights: Certified organic producer.
Nucha Malbec Orgánico among its notable wines, according to Wines of Argentina.

casa-gamboa-vinas-bodega.history: A vineyard planted in 2010 in Campana, near the Otamendi Nature Reserve and less than 70 km from the city of Buenos Aires. It grows Pinot Noir, Mourvèdre, Malbec, Cabernet Franc, Marselan and Cabernet Sauvignon.
highlights: Pinot Noir 2022: 94 points from Tim Atkin
Vineyard on clay soil beside the Otamendi Nature Reserve
casa-gamboa-vinas-bodega.flagship_grapes: Pinot Noir; 2022 vintage rated 94 points by Tim Atkin

casa-petrini.history: A wine tourism project in Tupungato, beside the Las Tunas River, combining a winery, a hotel with spa and a restaurant. It presents its wines as 'River Wines', linked to the river's terroir.
highlights: Winery with resort, spa and Enrico restaurant beside the Las Tunas River.

casa-yague.history: The winery of Marcelo Yagüe and Patricia Ferrari on route 259, in Trevelin, about 12 km from the Chilean border. It has 3 hectares and produces about 3,000 bottles a year of Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and a rosé.
highlights: One of the three most visited wineries in Trevelin
Equipped houses for four people beside the vineyard

casa-de-uco.history: A family project of the Tonconogy family in Los Chacayes combining its own vineyards, an experimental winery and a boutique hotel among the vineyards at the foot of the Andes.
highlights: Wine resort with suites, villas and residences among the vineyards.
Flora & Fauna, El Salvaje and El Salvaje Orgánico wines.

casarena.history: A winemaking project begun in 2007 after rebuilding a century-old family winery on Calle Brandsen, in Perdriel. It uses its own vineyards in Agrelo and Perdriel, including single-vineyard wines such as Jamilla, Lauren, Owen and Naoki.
highlights: Part of the Luján de Cuyo DOC.

cava-de-uco.history: A La Consulta winery created by four siblings in homage to their father, a grape grower who always wanted his own winery.
highlights: Family project of four siblings in homage to their grape-grower father.
Recipient of provincial wine tourism funding (2023)

cavas-del-artesano.history: A boutique family winery in the southern Atuel oasis, in General Alvear, whose first vintage was in 1959. It is led by Carlos Lalik, owner and winemaker, together with his son, with vineyards on the alluvial fan of the Atuel River.
highlights: Colección Pájaros Argentinos is one of its flagship ranges.
Uses indigenous yeasts and 12 to 18 months of bottle ageing.

cercano-sur.history: A winery 6 km from Espartillar, Coronel Suárez district, within an OIA-certified organic mixed-farming property with olive trees, almond trees and vineyards. It makes and estate-bottles Malbec, Cabernet Franc and Tannat.
highlights: Mixed-farming property with OIA organic certification

chaglasian-wine-suites.history: A project of Juan Chaglasian, of Armenian descent, that began in 2017 in San Rafael and combines a boutique winery, hotel and events hall. The rooms are above the winery, with glass floors looking down into the winemaking room.
highlights: It hosted the 2024 Fiesta Provincial de la Flor de la Vid.
Underground cellar about 5 metres deep.

chakana-ayni.history: Chakana was founded in 2002 in Agrelo by the Pelizzatti family, which left the project in 2019. In 2011 it bought the 25 ha Ayni estate in Paraje Altamira, source of its icon wine Vientre, first harvested in 2018.
highlights: Ayni Malbec among the three best Malbecs in the world at the Decanter World Wine Awards 2020.
Demeter biodynamic certification since 2016 (Finca Nuna, Agrelo).

champanera-cavas-de-zonda.history: A sparkling wine house built inside a hill in the Zonda Valley, about 16 km from the city of San Juan, accessed through a 200 m tunnel. The site was chosen for its stable temperature of 16 to 18 °C, suitable for making and storing sparkling wines.
highlights: Cellar inside a hill with a 200 m access tunnel
Sparkling wines from nature to sweet; visit with tasting and sales room

champanera-miguel-mas.history: A family sparkling wine house in Pocito, 11 km from the city of San Juan, making artisanal wines and sparkling wines by the traditional (champenoise) method. Its founder, Miguel Mas, is regarded as a pioneer of organic agriculture in Argentina and helped create its regulations.
highlights: Traditional-method (champenoise) sparkling wines, with disgorgement shown during the visit
Organic agriculture; member of the Slow Food Convivium Raíz de Cuyo
Quality distinction for wine tourism services (San Juan Wine Route)

cicchitti.history: José A. Cicchitti, grandson of Italian grape grower Giuseppe Mondati, founded Bodega Cicchitti in 1983 in Rodeo de la Cruz (Guaymallén). With the Cicchitti & Soigne brand it played a leading role in the growth of Argentine wine in the late 20th century.
highlights: Family winery with roots in Italian grape grower Giuseppe Mondati

cielos-de-gualjaina.history: A family winery founded in 2012 by two teachers in Gualjaina, Chubut, near the Piedra Parada reserve. It farms 1.5 hectares of Chardonnay, Gewürztraminer and Merlot with agroecological and biodynamic practices, in a building of adobe and river stone.
highlights: Agroecological and biodynamic practices
Winery built of adobe and river stone

clann-marangi.history: An artisanal winery in Cuadro Benegas, San Rafael, which in addition to wines makes other Malbec-based products.

conalbi-grinberg.history: A boutique wine house in Maipú, described as one of the first boutique wineries in Argentina. It offers tours and also operates as a bed & breakfast.

contra-corriente.history: A project started in 2013 by Americans Rance Rathie and Travis Smith 1 km from Trevelin. It produces about 10,000 bottles a year and also offers tastings with views of the Andes and accommodation beside the vineyard.
highlights: One of the three most visited wineries in Trevelin
Six rooms and a spa overlooking the vineyard

cooperativa-3-de-mayo.history: A growers' cooperative in Tres de Mayo (Lavalle) affiliated with Fecovita, the federation that brings together 29 Mendoza wine cooperatives.

cooperativa-vitivinicola-general-alvear.history: A General Alvear cooperative that operates Bodega La Regional, with more than half a century of growing grapes and making wines.

cooperativa-de-la-costa-de-berisso.history: A cooperative of small family growers on the Berisso coast that makes the traditional vino de la costa and organises the Fiesta Provincial del Vino de la Costa every July.
highlights: Organises the Fiesta Provincial del Vino de la Costa every July
An area of American grape varieties such as Isabella, on the banks of the Río de la Plata

cordon-blanco.history: A vineyard and winery in Tandil growing Carmenère, Syrah, Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon, Merlot and Cabernet Franc, with tours guided by winemaker Matías Lucas.
highlights: Two-hour vineyard tour with a tasting guided by the winemaker

cuncuna-bodega-cultural.history: An artisanal winery in Agua Blanca, Castro Barros department. It offers guided vineyard tours, tastings and a regional food courtyard by reservation.

del-rio-elorza.history: A boutique winery in General Fernández Oro that makes wine from grapes grown on its own estate in the Alto Valle del Río Negro.

dolium-bodega-subterranea.history: A small family business founded in 1997, with an underground winery in Agrelo. It is run by Ricardo Giadorou, second generation, with vineyards in Lunlunta, Agrelo, Perdriel and Chacras de Coria.
highlights: B Corp since 2014; it presents itself as the first Latin American winery with that certification.

domaine-le-billoud.history: A winery in Cruz de Piedra (Maipú) founded in 1890 by a family of French origin, from Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne. In 2019 it was run by Santiago Giraud Billoud, winemaker and sixth generation of the winemaking family.
highlights: Six generations of a winemaking family of French origin

domingo-hermanos.history: The Domingo family, who ran a transport business, received an estate with a vineyard as payment of a debt. It made its first wines in 1978 and in 1983 launched its demijohn, a fixture of the Serenata a Cafayate. It later added bottled ranges with no oak ageing.
highlights: Demijohn present at the Serenata a Cafayate
Reserva, Varietales and Regionales ranges
domingo-hermanos.flagship_grapes: Red blend: 60% Malbec, 30% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Tannat (2003 vintage)

don-milagro-cruz.history: A small winery at the back of a house in Purmamarca, facing the Cerro de los Siete Colores. It is run by Gastón Cruz, whose grandfather Milagro started the family tradition, with Criolla vines about 80 years old. Its best-known wine is Carnaval Torrontés.
highlights: Criolla vines about 80 years old
Quebrada de Humahuaca GI (recognised in 2015)
Took part in the La Nueva Ola – Vino de San Juan fair (Buenos Aires, 2022)
Recipient of provincial wine tourism funding (2023)

elefante-wines.history: Winery in Santa Lucía, in the Tulum Valley, offering tours that explain the winemaking process along with tastings of varietal wines. It also has a cantina and wine bar with simple menus paired with the house wines.
highlights: Cantina and wine bar on Fridays and Saturdays, by reservation
Winery tour with a tasting of varietal wines, Monday to Friday
elefante-wines.flagship_grapes: Malbec from Pedernal; fermented in steel tanks, 12 months in used barrels, unfiltered (2021 vintage)

elias-j-saleme.history: A winery in Tinogasta, Catamarca, that appears in Welcome Argentina's list with two entries: Elías Saleme in Santa Rosa and Elías J. Seleme S.A. on Avenida Córdoba.

entre-senderos.history: A growing project on the banks of the Futaleufú River, in Trevelin, that makes sparkling wine.

epsiloncru-vineyards.history: Chris Paulk bought about 19 acres in Las Paredes, San Rafael, in 2009 and planted three Malbec clones and one of Cabernet Sauvignon. He bottled his first wine, EpsilonCru, in 2013; the winemaker is Maxi Goulú.
highlights: Name inspired by the fifth star of the Southern Cross.
epsiloncru-vineyards.flagship_grapes: Single-block red, almost 2 years in French oak barrels

estilo-152.history: Five friends from General Acha began making wine in a garage and in 2016 registered the winery with the INV. In 2019 they planted an experimental vineyard in General Acha; the rest of the grapes come from Casa de Piedra. The name refers to National Route 152.
highlights: Boutique winery producing about 12,000 litres a year
Malbec Huellas del Caldenar, from a vineyard planted in 2019
estilo-152.flagship_grapes: Malbec from its own vineyard in General Acha

fow-fabricio-orlando-wines.history: Project of San Rafael winemaker Fabricio Orlando, who worked at Rutini and Pulenta Estate. Its hub is Finca El Maitén, in Cuadro Benegas, with a micro-winery, a restaurant in a 1900 manor house and an amphora room; it produces about 110,000 bottles a year.
highlights: Gold in the small wineries category, Best of Mendoza Wine Tourism 2026.
Malbec on alluvial sandy-loam soils of the Diamante River.
fow-fabricio-orlando-wines.flagship_grapes: Blend of Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon and Bonarda, aged in French oak barrels

famiglia-furfaro.history: Brothers Jorge and Hugo Furfaro planted their first vineyard in 2012 in Villa Ciudad Parque, Calamuchita, on a former potato field overlooking the Los Molinos reservoir. They produce about 21,000 bottles a year on 6 hectares.
highlights: Hillside vineyard facing the Los Molinos reservoir
Malbec, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay

familia-adrover.history: A small family winery founded in 2000, which restored a 1950s winery in Luján de Cuyo. It is known for affordable table wines, often sold in demijohns.

familia-blanco-wines.history: Mónica and Gabriel Blanco, from a farming family of Spanish origin, began working the land in the 1980s and in 2005 founded the winery with their five children. It makes the Familia Blanco and Mairena ranges.
highlights: Qatar Airways added one of the winery's Malbecs to its wine list.

familia-martinez-croce.history: A family company in Real del Padre that started in 1973, with its own vineyards in the area. After converting its vineyards to fine varieties, it has bottled varietals and sparkling wines since 2003.

highlights: Part of the Luján de Cuyo DOC.

familia-perulan.history: A family winery in Maipú, at Calle Bruno Morón 2347, whose winemaker and owner is Natalia Perulán. It makes varietals and blends on a small scale.

fecovita.history: The Federation of Argentine Wine Cooperatives was founded in October 1980 to unify the marketing of Mendoza cooperatives. In 1990 it bought the bottling unit of the former Bodega Giol and the Toro brand. Today it is the country's largest wine producer.
highlights: Brings together some 5,000 growers in 29 cooperatives, with 25,000 ha of vineyards
Owner of Toro, a brand created in 1890 by Gargantini and Giol
Argentina's largest wine producer, according to Bichos de Campo

finca-bodega-limbo.history: A winemaker's wine project of Osvaldo Asens and his wife María, begun in 2001 with the restoration of a 1930 Malbec estate in Cuadro Benegas. In 2007 they began making wine for their own consumption and later opened to tourism.
highlights: Old Malbec vineyard planted in 1930.
Bottles labelled by hand.

finca-agostino.history: Four brothers of Italian origin who grew up in Mendoza and emigrated to Canada in the 1960s returned in 2003 and bought vineyards in Barrancas (Maipú). There they make the Agostino wines, from Barrancas and El Cepillo grapes, and receive visitors with a restaurant and accommodation.
highlights: The group also includes Alfa Crux, in the Uco Valley, and the Telteca brand
finca-agostino.flagship_grapes: Malbec and Red Blend from the best grapes; 18 months in French oak and 12 in bottle

finca-albarossa.history: An estate founded in 2010 by the Italian family of Giacomo Spaini near Colalao del Valle. It makes Torrontés and Malbec under the Albarossa brand and has a restaurant and a wine-themed boutique hotel.
highlights: Themed boutique hotel among the vineyards
Restaurant by advance reservation, 11 am to 3 pm

finca-alta-bonanza-de-los-andes.history: An estate in Sorocayense, in the Calingasta-Barreal valley, at about 1,550 m altitude above the Los Patos River, sheltered to the east by the Precordillera. The winery emphasises its technical approach and winemaking in stainless steel tanks.
highlights: Vineyard at about 1,550 m beside the Los Patos River

finca-atos.history: A family project in the Calamuchita valley founded in 2002 by a couple and their three children. It has 9 hectares and produces about 20,000 bottles a year.

finca-bandini.history: A project of Federico Bandini, a Mendoza engineer based in Houston, who bought a 77-hectare property in Las Compuertas (Luján de Cuyo) to return to his homeland. The estate preserves 1922 irrigation sluice gates on the Mendoza River and is now a boutique winery with tours and a restaurant.
highlights: Vines at 1,070 m a.s.l. irrigated with snowmelt from the Mendoza River
The estate preserves irrigation sluice-gate structures dated 1922

finca-biodinamica-cosmos.history: An estate in Villa Tulumaya (Lavalle) founded in 2005 on the initiative of Laura Manzano, joined in 2012 by agronomist Raimundo Laugero. It practises biodynamic agriculture and has an artisanal winery making natural wines from traditional grapes.
highlights: Natural wines from Pedro Giménez, Torrontés Sanjuanino, Criolla varieties and Bonarda
Biodynamic management; 4 ha, of which 2 are vineyard

finca-concepcion-vinedos-sustentables.history: A sustainable vineyard in Sañogasta, Chilecito. It offers guided tours with tasting at weekends, a three-course menu and a picnic basket by reservation.

finca-decero.history: Finca Decero was born from the vision of Swiss businessman Thomas Schmidheiny. Its wines come from the Remolinos vineyard, in Agrelo, and seek to express the soil, climate and altitude of that estate.

finca-don-antonio.history: An estate in Balde de las Chilcas, in Valle Fértil, that presents itself as respectful of the environment and of artisanal traditions, and receives visitors to learn about its organic artisanal production.

finca-don-atilio.history: A 2-hectare vineyard in Cañuelas, 8 km from Uribelarrea, opened to tourism in December 2017. It grows Syrah, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir and Tannat.
highlights: Guided tours at weekends with a tasting of three wines

finca-don-diego.history: An estate founded in 1996 in San Pedro, in the Fiambalá valley, on land with vines 70 to 100 years old. Its name recalls three Diegos, including Diego Centurión, the owners' grandfather. It is known for its Syrah aged in chestnut barrels.
highlights: The country's first chestnut barrels, according to La Nación
Vines 70 to 100 years old in San Pedro

finca-dona-amanda.history: An estate in Colalao del Valle included in the Ruta del Vino de Altura of Tucumán. According to the official guide, it does not receive tourist visits.

finca-ivonne.history: A boutique winery in Real del Padre with limited production from its own vineyards, farmed sustainably by the family. Each bottle is sealed with wax by hand.

finca-la-anita.history: Founded in 1992 by Manuel Mas, who bought 72 hectares in Agrelo, it was one of the first premium boutique wineries in Argentina. Since late 2016 it has belonged to the Swiss group Origin Wine.

finca-la-macarena-sempiterno-wines.history: An estate and winery in Pocito, in the Tulum Valley, where the Sempiterno wines are made. It offers vineyard visits, a tour of the estate and winery, and a multi-course tapas menu paired with its wines, Thursdays and Fridays by reservation.
highlights: Multi-course tapas paired with house wines

finca-las-antipodas.history: An estate in Junín, Buenos Aires province, with Malbec and Cabernet Franc, offering weekend tastings and accommodation in containers overlooking the countryside.
highlights: Container accommodation overlooking the estate

finca-las-nubes.history: A small family winery in El Divisadero, above Cafayate, at the foot of the hills. It offers tours with tasting and simple meals. It now sells its wines together with Bodega Tukma at the Casa Tukma shop, with José Luis Mounier as winemaker.
highlights: Views of Cerro El Cajón and the Divisadero ruins

finca-las-payas.history: A mini-winery in the Las Paredes district created in 2005 by Santiago Salgado. It makes minimal-intervention natural wines in lots of 300 to 1,800 bottles, from uncommon grapes such as Criolla, Nero d'Avola, Corvina and Canarí.
highlights: Works with unusual varieties: Caladoc, Ancellotta, Patricia, Carignan and Gamay, among others.

finca-los-bayos.history: Jorge Riehme and his family planted the first Merlot and Chardonnay vines in 2017 on a 30-hectare estate in Urdinarrain, which also has pecan trees. They later added Marselan and Pinot Noir trials; the winemaker is his son Maximiliano.
highlights: Makes reds, whites, a rosé and a traditional-method sparkling wine
Combines vineyard with 15 hectares of pecan trees

finca-los-dragones.history: A winery, wine shop and wine bar in Barreal, Calingasta Valley. It offers free guided tours with tasting, by advance reservation.
highlights: Free guided tours with tasting, by reservation

finca-maria-del-pilar.history: The Luna family's winery in Higuera Chacra, near Beltrán, on a former goat farm. It planted vines from 2013 and opened the winery on 4 October 2019. Its wine was the first from Santiago del Estero certified by the INV.
highlights: First wine from Santiago del Estero certified by the INV
First harvest in January 2019
Makes Malbec and blends with Petit Verdot and Syrah

finca-mevi.history: Mevi was founded in 1991 as a venture of partners Oscar Vignart and Rolando Meninato, with an estate in eastern Mendoza. In 2009 they built a gravity-flow winery in Coquimbito (Maipú), with terraces for visits and tastings.
highlights: 2009 winery designed for gravity-flow winemaking, with minimal mechanical intervention

finca-montenieva.history: An estate in Seclantás, in the Calchaquí Valleys, included in Welcome Argentina's list of Salta wineries.

finca-organica-rincon-deseado.history: An organic, artisanal winery in San Rafael that also makes olive oil.

finca-sierras-azules.history: A family company at the foot of the Sierras Azules, in the Zonda Valley, at 780 m altitude, with a dry climate and a good diurnal temperature range. It makes the Summus range, with Tannat, Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec, Syrah, a blend and an orange wine, and receives visitors with tastings.
highlights: Summus range: Tannat, Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec, Syrah, a blend and an orange wine
Quality distinction for wine tourism services (San Juan Wine Route)
Recipient of provincial wine tourism funding (2023)

finca-suarez.history: A family project in Paraje Altamira, now in the hands of the fourth generation, with winemaker Juanfa Suárez. It farms 50 ha organically and biodynamically and uses part of the grapes for its own wines.
highlights: Fourth family generation in Paraje Altamira.
50 ha under organic and biodynamic management.

finca-vista-larga.history: A family ecological venture in the Huaco valley, Sanagasta, making high-altitude wines at 1,250 m a.s.l. It manages 80 ha of olive trees, walnut trees and vineyard with organic fertilisation.
highlights: Crops fertilised 100% with organic matter, according to the estate
More than 100 ha of preserved native woodland
Makes Bonarda, Chardonnay, Malbec and Torrontés

fincas-de-duval.history: A project in Gobernador Duval, on the banks of the Colorado River, that began in 2005 as an experimental farm. It has 3 hectares of Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Malbec and makes wine under the Lejanía label.
highlights: Also produces jams, preserves and olive oil

fisolo-vinedo-y-bodega-boutique.history: A family winery in Aldea María Luisa, Entre Ríos, started as a hobby by Raúl Fisolo and his son Matías, who expanded the vineyard in 2017. It is the only Entre Ríos winery devoted solely to sparkling wines, made by the traditional method from Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.
highlights: The only winery in Entre Ríos devoted exclusively to sparkling wines
Traditional-method sparkling wines, from Brut Nature to Dulce

gloria-galvagno-estate.history: A boutique family winery in Monte Comán, 15 minutes from San Rafael, born from Gloria Galvagno's project. It makes limited productions and combines tastings with glamping in domes among century-old vineyards.
highlights: Accommodation in glamping domes on the estate.

grazie-mille.history: A La Consulta winery that presents its production as 'Design Wines', with a focus on origin and a distinct identity.

gualtallary-wines.history: A Gualtallary winery that presents itself as a pioneer of high-altitude wines, with vineyards above 1,500 m. It makes the Gualtallary and Altus ranges and also has the La Tupiña restaurant and a four-room inn.
highlights: Altus Grand Vin 2020: 94 points and 'Revelation' in Descorchados.
Gualtallary Malbec 2018: 94 points James Suckling.
La Tupiña restaurant and 4-room inn.

hansen-becerra.history: A vineyard and winery in Lago Puelo, in the Comarca Andina, with Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Riesling.

huentala-wines.history: A project of Julio Camsen and his family in Gualtallary. Its Malbecs come from the La Isabel estate, where in 2019 they opened the first Sculpture Park among vineyards, with a 120-tonne work by Orlando Leytes.
highlights: Sculpture park in the vineyard of the La Isabel estate, since 2019.
Rastro restaurant on the estate.

ita-malal.history: A winery and vineyards in Abra del Hinojo, between Saavedra and Pigüé, growing Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon.
highlights: Open every day with tours and tastings by reservation

krontiras-wines.history: A project of Greek Constantino Krontiras and his Argentine wife Silvina, with an old-vine vineyard in Perdriel and another in Maipú. They have farmed organically since 2009 and biodynamically since 2012; since 2015 they have made reds without added sulphites.
highlights: Biodynamic since 2012, among the first in the country, according to Primal Wine.

la-caroyense.history: Founded in 1930 in Colonia Caroya as a cooperative of 34 Italians and opened in 1932, with a building reminiscent of Udine cathedral. After going bankrupt around 2000, it was auctioned in 2001 and passed to its current owners as a public limited company.
highlights: Traditional-method sparkling wines, Caroyense Piu range
Makes Lagrimilla, the traditional wine of the Friulian colony
Won 68 awards in competitions between 2009 and 2019

la-coste-de-los-andes.history: A Los Chacayes winery inspired by Château La Coste (France), with vineyards in Gualtallary, Los Chacayes and Alto Agrelo. It has been certified organic since 2014, ferments in concrete eggs and ages in French oak.
highlights: Organic certification since 2014.
Fermentation in concrete eggs and ageing in French oak.
Arauco restaurant at the winery.
la-coste-de-los-andes.flagship_grapes: Blend of the best plots of each vintage

la-guarida-del-malbec.history: A winery in the Pedernal Valley, Sarmiento department, owned by the Sánchez family, which settled on the estate to develop vineyards devoted exclusively to Malbec.
highlights: Vineyards exclusively of Malbec in the Pedernal Valley

la-matilde.history: A sustainable 60-hectare estate in Traslasierra, with its own vineyard, organic vegetable garden and a ten-room rural inn. The Malbec and Tannat vineyard was established with advice from Matías Michelini and is managed biodynamically.
highlights: Biodynamic management, according to Decanter
Ten-room rural inn
Recipient of provincial wine tourism funding (2023)

la-riojana-cooperativa-vitivinicola.history: A cooperative based in Chilecito that has operated since 1940. It brings together some 450 members, about 80% of the province's small and medium-sized growers. Its brands include Santa Florentina, Raza and Viñas Riojanas, and it exports organic wines.
highlights: Some 450 members from six La Rioja departments
Exports organic wines under the Pircas Negras, Origin and Ecológica brands
Makes a Torrontés Riojano sparkling wine

lamadrid-estate-wines.history: Guillermo García Lamadrid, born in Cuba, bought his first vineyards in Agrelo in 2004 and named the winery in homage to his mother, Matilde. In 2007 he acquired the Las Compuertas winery, next to an 1890 mansion.
highlights: A 1929 vineyard among its estates, according to the winery.

las-arcas-de-tolombon.history: A family winery in Colalao del Valle that the official tourism board presents as the largest premium wine venture in Tucumán. Its first label, Siete Vacas, recalls seven cows from the estate's history.
highlights: Siete Vacas range: Torrontés, Torrontés Tardío, Rosé, Naranjo and Tannat
Guided tours and tastings Monday to Saturday

las-canitas.history: A winery in the Calamuchita valley surrounded by pine woods and hills, with visits to the winemaking area and vineyard and a regional cuisine restaurant using produce from its garden.

las-flechas-group-finca-malligasta.history: An estate of Las Flechas Group in the Malligasta colonies, Chilecito. The group offers guided tours of the vineyard and production for groups of up to 10 people.

las-flechas-group-finca-vichigasta.history: A winery and vineyard of Las Flechas Group in Vichigasta, Chilecito, on Ruta 74. It offers guided tours of the vineyard and production, with tapas, Monday to Friday.

las-guapas.history: A boutique winery and restaurant in Chachingo (Maipú), with 5 hectares of century-old vineyards managed agroecologically. It produces limited lots of Malbec and presents itself as one of the smallest wineries in Mendoza.
highlights: Century-old Chachingo vineyards under agroecological management
las-guapas.flagship_grapes: Malbec from century-old vines; aged 100% in French oak

las-magnolias.history: A producer on the Gualeguaychú Wine Route, on the Acceso Sur, that grows Malbec, Tannat, Marselan and Sauvignon Blanc and makes reds, whites, a sweet wine and a sparkling wine.
highlights: Part of the Camino del Vino of Gualeguaychú

los-altares.history: A winery in the Chubut River valley, on route 25 in the Los Altares reserve, which Daniel Mileta started in memory of his son. It makes barrel-aged wines and a sparkling wine, about 3,000 to 4,000 bottles a year.
highlights: Displays dinosaur fossils, including eggs, at the winery

los-aromitos.history: A project of the Jacob family begun in 2011 in Colonia Ensayo, Diamante department, about 20 km from Paraná. It has about 3 hectares of vineyard and preserves 6 hectares of native woodland; it makes the Ará range.
highlights: Ará range: Tannat, Marselan, Malbec, Merlot, Syrah and Chardonnay
Preserves about 6 hectares of native woodland as a reserve

luna-de-cuarzo-biobodega.history: A small family winery in Colalao del Valle created by Silvia Gramajo, regarded as the first woman from Tucumán to develop her own venture on Ruta 40. It makes the Faustino del Pozo and Desata ranges, the latter organic.
highlights: First woman wine entrepreneur from Tucumán on Ruta 40
Organic Desata range
Fruit picking for visitors in season

maal-wines.history: MAAL was born in 2010 when friends Matías Fraga and winemaker Alfredo Merlo vinified six barrels with grapes from an abandoned vineyard. They make only Malbec. Their winery in Las Compuertas (Luján de Cuyo), built from recycled materials, had its first harvest in 2021.
highlights: Winery built from recycled containers, pipes and roofing
5 ha Las Compuertas estate at 980 m a.s.l., farmed organically
maal-wines.flagship_grapes: Malbec fermented in new barrels; limited edition of 900 bottles in exceptional years

mabellini-wines.history: A family project of Carlos Alberto Mabellini and Lorena Nicolás Creide, founded in 2018, which restored a century-old smallholding in Mainqué with vines planted in 1912 by the Verdecchia family. It also has a tasting space in the city of Neuquén.
highlights: Vineyards planted in 1912 by the Verdecchia family in Mainqué

martino-wines.history: Martino Wines bought an adobe winery built in 1901 in Luján de Cuyo in 2012, restored it and reopened it in 2013; it was expanded in 2015. It makes its own wines and also wines for other premium producers. Its Finca La Violeta, at 980 m a.s.l., has produced Malbec since 1926.
highlights: 1901 adobe-and-cane winery, restored in 2013
Finca La Violeta: Malbec since 1926, at 980 m a.s.l.

masi-tupungato.history: An Italian-Argentine project of Masi, a company with roots in the Veneto since 1773, begun in Tupungato in 1996. It organically grows Corvina and Pinot Grigio alongside Malbec and Torrontés, and uses a Veneto-style appassimento room.
highlights: Veneto-style appassimento (grape-drying) room.
Ageing in 600-litre Veronese casks.
Organic vineyards with Corvina, Pinot Grigio, Malbec and Torrontés.

media-hectarea.history: A collective artisanal wine project in Altamira, Mercedes, begun in 2011 and expanded with friends and family in 2012. Its name refers to the half hectare of vineyard and winery.
highlights: Visitors can take part in the harvest, racking and bottling

mil-suelos.history: Mil Suelos is the winery of agronomist Alejandro Sejanovich and Jeff Mausbach, with its base and restaurant in Chachingo (Maipú). It brings together projects from different regions, such as Teho, Buscado Vivo o Muerto, Manos Negras and the Huichaira vineyard in Jujuy.
highlights: Huichaira Vineyard, in the Quebrada de Humahuaca, at 2,750 m a.s.l.
mil-suelos.flagship_grapes: 1940 vines from Finca Tomal (4 ha, La Consulta); the source does not specify the varieties

myl-colores.history: A 2.5-hectare vineyard in the Sierras de Pillahuinco, Coronel Pringles, at 303 metres altitude, specialising in premium sparkling wines from Malbec, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Tannat.
highlights: Specialises in premium sparkling wines
Three suites overlooking the vineyard

ojo-de-agua.history: Founded in Agrelo by Swiss artist and musician Dieter Meier, of the duo Yello. It stands out for its organic production and makes the Puro and Ojo de Agua ranges.
highlights: Organic production.

patagonian-wines.history: The first vineyard and winery in Chubut, founded by Bernardo Weinert, owner of Cavas de Weinert, in El Hoyo, Comarca Andina. The land was bought in 1997 and the first vines were planted in 2000; the El Hoyo GI was recognised at his request.
highlights: First vineyard and winery in the province of Chubut
Drove the recognition of the El Hoyo GI
Piedra Parada and Faldeo del Epuyén ranges, and Más Allá sparkling wine

posada-y-bodega-apotema.history: A project of Eduardo Ranea in Villa Basilio Nievas, Zonda, begun in 2002 making bulk wine for large wineries. Today it bottles all its production, about 45,000 litres a year, from 7 ha of its own. It registered the vineyard to use the Valle de Zonda GI.
highlights: 7 ha vineyard: Syrah, Malbec, Petit Verdot and Viognier
Wines with the Valle de Zonda Geographical Indication
Hosts guests, mainly European tourists (2021)

puerta-oeste.history: An artisanal family winery in Senillosa, Neuquén, run by Viviana and Julio, offering vineyard visits with tasting.

punta-de-los-venados.history: A vineyard started in 2012 by a group of investors near Candelaria, San Luis, on provincial route 79. It has 10 drip-irrigated hectares surrounded by native woodland and makes the Célebres Puntanos range, named after figures from San Luis history.
highlights: Bronze medal at the Bonarda Argentina 2017 competition
Célebres Puntanos range: Blend, Bonarda, Malbec, Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon

rivier-vinas-y-bodegas.history: A family company founded in 1956 by Jean Rivier, a Swiss immigrant from Lausanne. Under the motto 'Viticultores Criadores', it vinifies grapes from its own vineyards in San Rafael and the Uco Valley.
highlights: Visits with tasting in its underground cellar and the Vinotest pairing game.

rosell-boher.history: In 1999 the premises of a winery founded in the late 19th century by Bernardo Martínez, grandfather of winemaker Alejandro Martínez Rosell, were restored. It makes sparkling wines solely by the champenoise method, as well as still wines such as the Casa Boher range.
highlights: Great Wine Capitals Best Of 2020: Best Winery Restaurant in the World.
Gold in Sustainable Practices 2023, Great Wine Capitals.
Lodge in Alto Agrelo with 11 private villas and a spa.

rio-piedras-finca-y-bodega.history: An estate in El Mogote, Chimbas, in the Tulum Valley, offering a tour of the vineyards and the old main building of the former Bodega Río Piedras.
highlights: Tour of the old main building of the former Bodega Río Piedras

rio-del-medio.history: A small winery of Carlos and Laura Testa in Los Reartes, Calamuchita valley, where Sauvignon Blanc is the star variety.
highlights: Malabar Sauvignon Blanc, Revelation of Argentina 2021 in Descorchados
rio-del-medio.flagship_grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Revelation of Argentina 2021 in Descorchados

secreto-patagonico.history: One of the smallest wineries in San Patricio del Chañar, owned by the Groppo family. It sits at the top of the vineyard, allowing gravity-flow winemaking, and its premium wines have reached export standards.
highlights: Gravity-flow winemaking from the top of the vineyard

selada-wines.history: The winery of winemaker Osvaldo Selada, a graduate of the Don Bosco Faculty, in Guaymallén, making winemaker's wines. It works with grapes from different parts of Mendoza, between 900 and 1,250 m a.s.l., and is geared towards wine tourism.
highlights: 250,000-litre winery with ageing in French oak barrels

sorocayo-finca-basin.history: An estate and winery in Sorocayense, Calingasta, making mountain wines. It offers guided tours with tasting and sales of high-altitude wines, by advance reservation.
highlights: Took part in the La Nueva Ola – Vino de San Juan fair (2022)
Recipient of provincial wine tourism funding (2023)

staphyle.history: A winery created in 1927 as a small venture in Carrodilla, now equipped with modern technology and a capacity of 730,000 litres.

terra-camiare.history: A Colonia Caroya winery with roots in Italian immigrants, founded in 1928 according to Decanter. It uses only Córdoba grapes, ferments in cement eggs and produces the Socavones range.
highlights: Uses only Córdoba grapes, including old Isabella vines
Socavones Capitulum Sémillon, from Quilino grapes

territorios-trilla.history: A winemaker's wine project with a recently opened garage winery in Alto Verde, San Martín. It uses hand-harvested grapes from its vineyards in Alto Verde and Algarrobo Grande (Junín).
highlights: Grows Malbec, Ancellotta, Petit Verdot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc.

tierra-colorada-desvario.history: A family winery on the Estancia Chimpa, on Ruta 68 near Cafayate, now in the hands of the fourth generation. The 7,500 ha estancia reaches the Cafayate dunes and has an 1890 mansion with five rooms.
highlights: 7,500 ha estancia with access to the Cafayate dunes
1890 mansion with five rooms

trez-wines.history: Founded in Mendoza in 2007 by three partners, Roberto Timms, Jorge Ramírez and Esteban Zombory, whose surnames form the name TREZ. It aims for limited-production wines made with practices from the European tradition.

uraqui-claudio-zucchino.history: An organic project of Claudio Zucchino in Uquía, with an inn and a small winery. He ages his wines in an abandoned mine where his father worked, at almost 4,000 m a.s.l., and his Moya vineyard is at 3,329 m a.s.l. The Uraqui Minero wine pays homage to his father.
highlights: Tim Atkin: 96 points for Uraqui Minero Corte A 2016 (Argentina Report 2018)
Moya vineyard at 3,329 m a.s.l. and a cellar in a mine at almost 4,000 m
Organic grapes
uraqui-claudio-zucchino.flagship_grapes: Organic Malbec, Syrah and Merlot; unoaked, aged in mine galleries

valle-arriba.history: A project of agronomists Raúl Dávalos, from a Salta family with six generations in wine, and Paula Marra. From 2006 Dávalos planted seven vineyards in Angastaco, Molinos, Seclantás and Cachi; Marra joined in 2017. Its base is the Las Carreras estate, in Cachi Adentro.
highlights: Pinot Noir planted at 2,500 m in Molinos
About 40,000 bottles a year
valle-arriba.flagship_grapes: Grapes from an estate west of Angastaco; Valle de Pucará GI (2025)

vinos-adentro.history: A project with a vineyard in Cachi that makes wine in rented facilities in Colomé while it builds its own winery. Its wines are served in Cachi restaurants; it has a Torrontés.

vista-grande.history: A project of the Martinelli family in the Los Reartes area, Calamuchita valley, which began as Daniel's hobby and is now led by his daughter Daniela. Planting began in 2018, and the winery makes nine labels.
highlights: Surmenage, a Roussanne and Chardonnay blend, highlighted by Decanter
About 14,000 bottles a year across nine labels

vina-el-cerno.history: An artisanal family winery in Coquimbito (Maipú), founded in 1996 and run by parents and children. It makes organic, natural and vegan wines, and its building preserves carved doors brought from France.
highlights: Organic, natural and vegan winemaking, according to the winery

vina-las-perdices.history: The Muñoz López family winery in Agrelo; its name recalls Juan Muñoz, who was accompanied by partridges while working his vines. It has its own 96-hectare estate with more than 17 varieties and almost 70 labels.

vinas-puntanas.history: A project of the Buenos Aires Quiroga Hourcade family, conceived by Manuel Quiroga, in Bajo de Véliz, in the Conlara valley, about 20 km from Merlo. The first harvest was in 2010.
highlights: Gold for its Tannat and silver for its Syrah at Vinus 2010

vinas-del-perchel.history: A family winery between Tilcara and Huacalera that presents itself as a pioneer in planting fine varieties in the Quebrada de Humahuaca. Javier Vargas planted the vineyard around 2007, and his sister Mabel runs the venture. It makes the Cactus range and the Runa blend.
highlights: Cactus Tannat, 100% Tannat
Quebrada de Humahuaca GI (recognised in 2015)

vinas-y-bodegas-graffigna-yanzon.history: A winery in the Pedernal Valley, on National Route 153, in Sarmiento department. It belongs to the group of wineries with a quality distinction for wine tourism services on the San Juan Wine Route.
highlights: Pedernal Valley: GI recognised in 2017, vineyards above 1,400 m
Quality distinction for wine tourism services (San Juan Wine Route)

vinedos-yacoraite.history: A high-altitude vineyard in Yacoraite, Quebrada de Humahuaca, at 2,777 m a.s.l., owned by economist Alejandro Izquierdo. Its wine Mallku is a Malbec made with winemaker Lucas Niven.
highlights: Notable winery architecture at extreme altitude, according to the national tourism board
Quebrada de Humahuaca GI (recognised in 2015)

vinedos-del-viento-agua-de-fuego.history: A winery on national route 22, about 118 km from the city of Neuquén, in Cutral Có, with the Agua de Fuego restaurant for about 100 diners and a pairing offering.
highlights: Agua de Fuego restaurant with capacity for 100 diners

bodega-salentein.history: Dutch businessman Mijndert Pon bought the estate in 1996 and began planting vineyards. In 1997 he planted Malbec at 1,300 m, one of the first high-altitude plantings in the Uco Valley, and in 1998 the winery's foundation stone was laid.
highlights: Ranked 12th in The World's 50 Best Vineyards.
Posada Salentein: 16 rooms and a restaurant serving Cuyo regional cuisine.
Killka cultural centre, with Argentine and Dutch art, inside the winery.

bodega-trapiche.history: Founded in 1883 by Tiburcio Benegas, who named his estate El Trapiche. In 1971 it passed to the Pulenta family (Peñaflor) and today it is part of Grupo Peñaflor. Its Renaissance-style building in Coquimbito dates from 1912.
highlights: Twice named Argentine Producer of the Year at the International Wine & Spirit Competition
World's Most Admired Argentine winery according to Drinks International (2017)
Renaissance-style building from 1912, an icon of Argentine winery architecture
bodega-trapiche.flagship_grapes: Premium blends in two versions: Syrah-Viognier and Malbec-Cabernet Franc

altos-las-hormigas.history: Founded in 1995 by Italian winemaker Alberto Antonini and businessman Antonio Morescalchi, it was one of the first wineries to focus on Malbec in Mendoza. Today it is led by Mendoza-born winemaker Federico Gambetta, with an emphasis on organic and regenerative viticulture.
highlights: Certified organic, according to Skurnik.
Single-vineyard Malbecs from Altamira (1,200 m a.s.l.) and Gualtallary (1,300 m a.s.l.).

bodega-diamandes.history: The Bonnie family, owners of Château Malartic-Lagravière in Bordeaux, arrived in the Uco Valley in 2005 as part of the Clos de los Siete project. It has made wine since the 2007 vintage in a Bordeaux-influenced style.
highlights: Part of the Clos de los Siete project in Vista Flores.
Makes organic and vegan wines with sustainable practices, according to Mendoza tourism.
DIAM'S Bistrot & Bar à Vin restaurant, opened in 2017.
bodega-diamandes.flagship_grapes: Red (blend, grapes not disclosed) and Chardonnay with 14 months in French oak, 60% new

terrazas-de-los-andes.history: Founded in 1996 by Moët Hennessy, it grew out of the exploration of high-altitude vineyards begun in the early 1990s by French viticulturist Hervé Birnie-Scott. It farms more than 200 high-altitude plots and puts Malbec front and centre. In 1999 it partnered with Château Cheval Blanc to create Cheval des Andes.
highlights: Organic and regenerative viticulture, according to the winery.
Six-room guesthouse and a restaurant serving regional cuisine.
Member of the DOC Luján de Cuyo.
terrazas-de-los-andes.flagship_grapes: Single-parcel Malbec: Los Cerezos (Las Compuertas, planted 1929) and Los Castaños (Paraje Altamira)

susana-balbo-wines.history: Winemaker Susana Balbo founded the winery in 1999 in Agrelo under the name Dominio del Plata. It produces the Crios, BenMarco, Susana Balbo and Nosotros brands. Balbo has twice served as president of Wines of Argentina.
highlights: Nosotros Malbec 2008: 94 points in The Wine Advocate (December 2011).
Osadía de Crear restaurant and Argentine cooking classes.
susana-balbo-wines.flagship_grapes: Malbec from Agrelo, a selection of the 40 best barrels; 16–18 months in new French oak

bodega-mendel.history: Mendel was born in 2002, when the Sielecki family bought an old winery in Mayor Drummond (Luján de Cuyo) and brought in winemaker Roberto de la Mota as a partner. It works vineyards in Mayor Drummond, Perdriel and Finca Remota, in Paraje Altamira (Uco Valley).
highlights: Finca Mendel Malbec planted in 1928 in Mayor Drummond, at 950 m a.s.l.
Finca Remota in Paraje Altamira at 1,040 m a.s.l., with vines from 1947
Alluvial soils, very stony and free-draining, according to the winery
bodega-mendel.flagship_grapes: Blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Malbec

bodega-norton.history: Founded in 1895 by English engineer Edmund James Palmer Norton, who planted the first vineyard south of the Mendoza River in Perdriel. In 1989 it was bought by Austrian businessman Gernot Langes-Swarovski. According to the winery, its Malbec was the first exported to the United States, in 1973.
highlights: Its winemaker David Bonomi was Tim Atkin's Winemaker of the Year in 2021.
La Vid restaurant and tastings in the historic cellar.
Member of the DOC Luján de Cuyo.

bodega-matervini.history: Matervini is the project of Santiago Achával and Italian winemaker Roberto Cipresso, co-founders of Achaval Ferrer. It was created in 2008 to show how Malbec changes with terroir, including non-alluvial soils in the Precordillera.

bodega-superuco.history: Project of the Michelini brothers begun in 2011 with 2 hectares in Los Chacayes, within The Vines of Mendoza. It works with organic and biodynamic farming, and the winery is an octagon at the centre of the estate.
highlights: Gold for Sustainable Practices, Best of Wine Tourism 2021 (Great Wine Capitals).
Biodynamically farmed vineyard, with a vegetable garden and animal pens in a circular layout.
Located in Los Chacayes, Tunuyán, at about 1,200 m.

bodega-familia-schroeder.history: Founded in 2001 by Herman Schroeder and his children in San Patricio del Chañar, Neuquén. During construction, the remains of a dinosaur later named Panamericansaurus schroederi were found, inspiring the Saurus range.
highlights: Discovery of the dinosaur Panamericansaurus schroederi during construction
Saurus restaurant, serving some 10,000 diners a year
Receives some 15,000 visitors a year, according to Forbes

michelini-i-mufatto.history: Family project of Gerardo Michelini and Andrea Mufatto, who returned from Spain to Mendoza in 2005 to make their own wines. They make wine at La Cantina in Tupungato, and since 2015 also in El Bierzo (Spain) and since 2019 in Uruguay.
highlights: They ferment in reclaimed old oak vats and in concrete amphorae
Winemaking in three countries: Argentina, Spain (El Bierzo) and Uruguay

escala-humana-wines.history: Project of Germán Masera, a winemaker with experience in Mendoza, the United States, Spain and Patagonia, and Ayelén Bonetto. Their Livverá range was launched in 2015. In Gualtallary they have La Masía, the farm where they live and work.
highlights: Three ranges: Livverá, Geografía Extraordinaria and CREDO.
Visits Monday to Friday from 9 am to 4 pm; other times by appointment.

bodega-los-toneles.history: Urban winery in Guaymallén built in 1922 (formerly Armando Hermanos). The Millán family bought it in 2002, restored it and resumed winemaking in 2010. Today it is a Cultural Heritage site of Mendoza and has a restaurant, café and art gallery.
highlights: Familia Millán was named Winery of the Year in the Descorchados 2024 guide
Declared Cultural Heritage of Mendoza; celebrated its centenary in 2022
Abrasado restaurant, specialising in dry-aged meats
bodega-los-toneles.flagship_grapes: Malbec from Los Chacayes (Tunuyán), 16–18 months in new oak

bemberg-estate-wines.history: After selling Cervecería Quilmes in 2010, the Bemberg family invested in winemaking by buying Grupo Peñaflor. Its winery on the El Tomillo estate, in Gualtallary, has made the Pionero and La Linterna ranges since the 2013 vintage.
highlights: Top ranges Pionero and La Linterna; winemaking by Daniel Pi (Los Andes, 2020).
Finca El Tomillo: 68 ha at 1,210 m in Gualtallary.
Tours with tastings facing the Tupungato volcano, according to Mendoza tourism.
bemberg-estate-wines.flagship_grapes: Bordeaux blend (a tribute to Otto Peter Bemberg)

humberto-canale.history: Humberto Canale arrived in General Roca in 1909, bought 600 hectares and planted vines and fruit trees. Having no children, the business passed to his nephew Manuel Luis Canale and later to the Barzi family; it now spans four generations.
highlights: Vines planted in 1937, among the oldest in Patagonia
Four generations at the head of the winery
Premium wines: Galgos, Barzi Canale and Dos Cielos
humberto-canale.flagship_grapes: Blend of Malbec 37%, Merlot 33%, Cabernet Franc 19% and Petit Verdot 11% (Alto Valle de Río Negro)

bodega-del-fin-del-mundo.history: A project driven by Julio Viola in San Patricio del Chañar, Neuquén: the first vineyards were planted around 1999 and winemaking began in 2003. In 2019 the assets were split and the winery went to Corporación América (Eurnekian group), while the Viola family continued with Malma.
highlights: First and largest winery in San Patricio del Chañar according to Diario Río Negro
Owned by Corporación América (Eurnekian group) since 2019
bodega-del-fin-del-mundo.flagship_grapes: Blend of Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, aged in French oak barrels

bodega-xumek.history: A Zonda Valley project with two estates: Santa Sylvia, of about 150 ha, and La Ciénaga, of about 50 ha at close to 1,500 m altitude. In 2019 it opened the estate to controlled visits and was planning its own winery, with artworks such as a whale by Adrián Villar Rojas.
highlights: Main varieties at Santa Sylvia: Syrah, Malbec, Tannat, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc
Winemaker: Daniel Ekkert (Tiempo de San Juan, 2019)
bodega-xumek.flagship_grapes: Malbec from La Ciénaga (Zonda); a few months in 500 L barrels and 6 months in bottle

bodega-tapiz.history: Since 2003 Tapiz has belonged to Fincas Patagónicas, owned by the Ortiz family, which bought it from the US company Kendall-Jackson. The group also owns Zolo and Wapisa; according to its tourism listing, only Zolo receives visitors.

bodega-miras.history: Family winery of Mendoza-born winemaker Marcelo Miras, based in Río Negro since 1990, when he joined Humberto Canale. In 2017 he bought a farm in Mainqué with vines planted in 1958, under certified organic management; his five children take part in the business.
highlights: Vines planted in 1958 in Mainqué, with certified organic grapes
Makes Trousseau, a variety rarely found in Argentina
Exports to Canada, the United States, Brazil, England and Germany

domaine-bousquet.history: The Bousquet family, with four generations of winemaking tradition in the south of France, settled in Gualtallary in 1997. Since its first vintage in 2002 it has made 100% organic wines and now adds biodynamic and regenerative practices.
highlights: Organic wines since its first vintage, in 2002.
Regenerative Organic Certified (ROC); it presents itself as the first Argentine winery to hold this certification.
Gaia Restaurante and Gaia Lodge on the estate.
domaine-bousquet.flagship_grapes: Top range: Malbec Single Vineyard 100% Malbec and a blend (60% Malbec, 20% Cabernet Sauvignon, 10% Merlot, 10% Syrah), 16 months in French oak; biodynamic

bodega-andeluna.history: Andeluna was born in 2003 from a partnership between the Reina Rutini family and American Ward Lay. In 2013 it was bought by the Barale family, who also own La Soñada in southern Mendoza. It makes high-altitude wines in Gualtallary.
highlights: Alluvial soils that were seabed some 100 million years ago, according to the winery.
Restaurant, tastings and Andeluna Winery Lodges.
Present in more than 30 international markets.
bodega-andeluna.flagship_grapes: Gualtallary range in very limited releases; Malbec and Cabernet Franc versions

bodega-chandon.history: Chandon Argentina began in 1959 at the initiative of Robert-Jean de Vogüé of Moët & Chandon, who, together with Champagne winemaker Renaud Poirier, chose Agrelo to make sparkling wines. Since then it has sought ever-higher vineyards, with estates in the Uco Valley since 1994.

flechas-de-los-andes.history: Partnership between Benjamin de Rothschild (Château Clarke) and Laurent Dassault (Château Dassault), from Bordeaux. The name refers to the five arrows on the Rothschild coat of arms. Its 102 ha vineyard in Vista Flores was planted in 1999.
highlights: 102 ha vineyard in 48 plots, planted in 1999.
Alluvial soils of stones, sand and clay, poor in organic matter.
Gran range: Gran Malbec, Gran Cabernet Franc and Gran Corte.

ernesto-catena-vineyards.history: Founded in 2000 in Vista Flores by Ernesto Catena, of the fourth generation of a family of grape growers of Italian origin. The estate is certified organic and biodynamic, and its buildings are inspired by pre-Columbian architecture. It groups the brands Alma Negra, Tikal Natural, Ánimal and Siesta en el Tahuantinsuyu.
highlights: Estate certified organic and biodynamic, according to the winery.
Ernesto Catena, fourth generation of grape growers of Italian origin.
Brands: Alma Negra, Tikal Natural, Ánimal and Siesta en el Tahuantinsuyu.

bodega-malma.history: Winery of the Viola family in San Patricio del Chañar, operated by Viñedos de la Patagonia SRL. The family, pioneers of Neuquén wine with vineyards planted since 1999, separated from Bodega del Fin del Mundo in 2019 and continued independently with Malma, led by Ana Viola.
highlights: Uses only grapes from its own vineyards; exports about 50%
Awarded the Vitivinicultura Argentina Sostenible seal

vinas-del-nant-y-fall.history: The Rodríguez family arrived in Trevelin in 2009 and in 2010 planted their first Pinot Noir vines; the first harvest was in 2016. Sergio Rodríguez is the founder and his son Emmanuel runs the vineyard and winery.
highlights: More than 20 Tim Atkin gold medals, according to Forbes
In the Trevelin GI, the first in Chubut (2020)
Receives some 20,000 visitors a year

bodega-tacuil.history: Winery of the Dávalos family in the Tacuil valley, southwest of Molinos. Its tradition dates back to the 19th century, when Ascensión Isasmendi de Dávalos introduced Malbec to Salta. Today it is run by the sixth generation, with Raúl Dávalos and his brother Álvaro as winemaker.
highlights: Sixth generation of the Dávalos family at the helm
12 ha of Sauvignon Blanc, Torrontés, Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon
Vineyards between 2,400 and 2,700 m a.s.l.

bodega-vasija-secreta.history: Founded in 1857 by Camila Quintana de Niño, on land that had belonged to Nicolás Aramburu, and later known as La Banda. Vicente Murga bought it in 1957; his daughter Nelly Murga de Córdova created the museum in 1970, and the winery was renamed Vasija Secreta in 2000.
highlights: La Banda 1857 Museum with old barrels, machinery and tools
Retains part of its old vineyards
Makes Torrontés, Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon and Tannat

bodegas-callia.history: Winery in the Tulum Valley created by the Salentein group to add San Juan as a second terroir alongside Mendoza. With winemaker Óscar Biondolillo, from 2003 it saw strong commercial growth known as the 'Callia phenomenon', based on its value for money.
highlights: Vineyards in the Tulum, Ullum, Pedernal and Zonda valleys
Magna premium range (Syrah and Malbec)

bodega-michango.history: Winery of the Andreatta family, of Italian origin, who have made wine in Catamarca since the late 19th century. The current winery, now called Michango, was built in 1968 in the provincial capital; the vineyard is in Siján, in the Pomán valley. It is run by Oscar Andreatta, the fifth generation.
highlights: Fifth generation of the Andreatta family
Organic certification obtained in 2022
Makes Malbec, Bonarda, Torrontés, a sparkling wine and a naturally sweet Muscat of Alexandria

puerta-del-abra.history: Project of Jorge Pérez Companc, through La Gloriosa SA, begun in 2013 in El Vallecito, between Balcarce and Mar del Plata. It has 12 hectares with seven varieties in production since 2016, and at its request the Balcarce GI was recognised in 2022.
highlights: Promoted the Balcarce GI, recognised in 2022 (Resolution 11/2022)
El Insólito Velo de Flor Chardonnay 2020: 94 points, James Suckling Top 100
Itzae White Blend I 2024: 95 points from Tim Atkin (Argentina Report 2026)

finca-la-celia.history: Eugenio Bustos planted the estate's first Malbec in 1882 and built the winery in 1890 in San Carlos, Uco Valley. In 1998 it was bought by the Chilean group Viña San Pedro, which expanded and restored the winery the following year. Soil studies in 2013 and 2023 guided its plot-specific wines.
highlights: First Malbec planted on the estate in 1882; winery built in 1890.
Owned by the Chilean group Viña San Pedro since 1998.
Soil studies in 2013 and 2023 to make plot-specific wines.
finca-la-celia.flagship_grapes: Three 1 ha single-plot wines, 2019 vintage: Malbec, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon (2,000 bottles each)
